requirements.title: Understanding the Organization and Its Context
requirements.intent: Organization identifies internal and external issues relevant to QMS purpose and strategic direction.
expected_evidence: Context analysis documented (SWOT, PESTLE, or equivalent)
failure_modes: generic boilerplate with no organization-specific content
issues not linked to QMS scope or risk planning

requirements.title: Needs and Expectations of Interested Parties
requirements.intent: Organization identifies interested parties (customers, regulators, employees, suppliers, certification bodies) and their relevant requirements.
failure_modes: regulatory bodies (FAA, EASA, CAAC) not listed

requirements.title: Determining Scope of the QMS
requirements.intent: Scope is defined, documented, and maintained. Exclusions are justified. Scope references applicable regulatory requirements.
failure_modes: regulatory requirements not referenced in scope
scope does not match OASIS registration

requirements.title: Scope Exclusions (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: If clause 8.3 (Design and Development) is excluded, the justification must demonstrate the organization has no design responsibility and the exclusion does not affect conformity.
expected_evidence: explanation of why exclusion does not affect product conformity
failure_modes: Design exclusion claimed with no justification
organization performs some design activities but claims full 8.3 exclusion
exclusion not reviewed when scope changes
requirements.applicability: Only required when design exclusion is claimed.

requirements.title: QMS and Its Processes
requirements.intent: Organization determines, documents, and manages the processes needed for the QMS, including their sequence, interactions, criteria, resources, responsibilities, risks, and opportunities.
failure_modes: Process map is purely organizational chart

requirements.title: Leadership and Commitment
requirements.intent: Top management demonstrates commitment through active involvement, not just signing a policy. Includes customer focus responsibilities.
expected_evidence: quality objectives signed by top management
evidence of top management participation in QMS activities
failure_modes: Leadership section is generic policy statements only
customer focus is a statement with no mechanism

requirements.title: Quality Policy
requirements.intent: Quality policy is appropriate to the organization, includes commitment to requirements and continual improvement, provides framework for objectives.
failure_modes: no reference to customer or regulatory requirements
not communicated beyond document control folder
doc_types: Quality Policy (standalone or embedded in Quality Manual)

requirements.title: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
requirements.intent: Roles and authorities are assigned, communicated, and understood. Includes responsibility for product conformity, customer focus, and QMS integrity.
expected_evidence: job descriptions linked to QMS roles
failure_modes: Org chart only — no responsibilities defined
"quality department responsible for all quality" with no specificity
roles undefined for key QMS activities

requirements.title: Actions to Address Risks and Opportunities
requirements.intent: Organization identifies risks and opportunities; plans actions; evaluates effectiveness. Must be systematic, not reactive.
failure_modes: Risk register is a one-time exercise never updated
only product risk assessed (not QMS/process risk)

requirements.title: Risk Management (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Organization applies a formal risk management process (not just risk thinking). Process must be consistent, proportionate to risk, and applied to all relevant areas including product/process safety, counterfeit parts, and configuration.
expected_evidence: risk methodology (FMEA, fault tree, risk matrix)
failure_modes: "Risk thinking" documented with no formal process
risk management applied only to projects

requirements.title: Quality Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them
requirements.intent: Quality objectives are measurable, monitored, communicated, and updated. Plans to achieve them include who, what, when, and how measured.

requirements.title: Planning of Changes
requirements.intent: Changes to the QMS are planned, considering purpose, integrity, resource availability, and responsibility allocation.
failure_modes: Ad hoc changes to QMS procedures with no control

requirements.title: Planning of Changes (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Changes to products and processes are controlled with specific aerospace rigor: impact on configuration, airworthiness, customer approval, and regulatory notification evaluated before implementation.
expected_evidence: validation of changed process before release
failure_modes: Only QMS document changes controlled — product/process changes uncontrolled
no customer notification for changes affecting approved data
requirements.applicability: All organizations — critical for production and MRO.

requirements.title: General Resources
requirements.intent: Organization determines and provides resources for QMS implementation, maintenance, and improvement.
failure_modes: No evidence resources are formally determined
reactive resource allocation with no planning

requirements.title: People
requirements.intent: Adequate, competent personnel are provided for QMS operation and control.
expected_evidence: personnel records linked to QMS roles
failure_modes: competency not linked to QMS requirements

requirements.title: Infrastructure
requirements.intent: Infrastructure (buildings, equipment, utilities, transport, IT) is determined, provided, and maintained to support product conformity.

requirements.title: Environment for the Operation of Processes
requirements.intent: Work environment is managed to the extent it affects product conformity (cleanliness, temperature, humidity, ESD, FOD control, lighting).
failure_modes: FOD prevention not addressed for applicable processes
requirements.applicability: All organizations — FOD specifically required for aerospace hardware.

requirements.title: Monitoring and Measuring Resources
requirements.intent: Measurement equipment is identified, calibrated, maintained, and traceable to national/international standards.
requirements.applicability: All organizations with measurement equipment used to verify product conformity.

requirements.title: Measurement Traceability (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Calibration traceability is established and maintained to national or international measurement standards. Where no such standards exist, basis of calibration is documented.
failure_modes: Calibration performed without establishing traceability chain
certificates do not reference national standards
internal standards not calibrated against traceable references
requirements.applicability: All organizations with calibrated measurement equipment.

requirements.title: Calibration/Verification Records (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Calibration records capture: equipment ID, calibration date, results, out-of-tolerance findings, and adjustment information.
expected_evidence: Complete calibration records with all required fields
customer notification when out-of-tolerance discovered retrospectively
failure_modes: no product recall assessment when equipment found out of tolerance

requirements.title: Organizational Knowledge
requirements.intent: Organization determines, maintains, and makes available the knowledge needed for process operation and product conformity. Considers lessons learned and new knowledge acquisition.
expected_evidence: retention strategy for departing personnel knowledge
failure_modes: lessons learned not captured or not fed back to planning
no process for capturing expert knowledge

requirements.title: Competence
requirements.intent: Personnel affecting quality conformity are competent. Competency based on education, training, or experience. Effectiveness of training evaluated.
expected_evidence: qualification records for special process operators
failure_modes: Training records exist but effectiveness never evaluated
competency matrix not linked to job roles or QMS requirements
on-the-job training (OJT) sign-offs with no criteria

requirements.title: Competence — Aerospace Addition
requirements.intent: Personnel performing special processes (welding, NDT, heat treat, etc.) must be qualified and certified to applicable standards (NAS410, AWS, etc.). Records of qualifications maintained.
expected_evidence: Certifier/qualification records per applicable specification (e.g., NAS 410 for NDT, AWS D17.1 for welding)
failure_modes: Special process operators not certified to applicable standards
personnel performing processes beyond their certification scope
requirements.applicability: Required when special processes are in scope.

requirements.title: Awareness
requirements.intent: Personnel are aware of quality policy, objectives, their contribution to QMS effectiveness, and implications of noncompliance.

requirements.title: Communication
requirements.intent: Internal and external communication relevant to the QMS is determined and executed (what, when, with whom, how).
expected_evidence: examples of internal communications (QMS changes, policy updates)
failure_modes: customer communications handled informally with no documentation

requirements.title: Documented Information
requirements.intent: Required documented information is created, controlled, and maintained. Includes all documents and records required by the standard and the organization.

requirements.title: Configuration Management in Documented Information (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Documented information is controlled such that configuration of products and processes can be determined from records. Linkage between drawing revision, process revision, and product configuration maintained.
failure_modes: Drawing revisions not linked to production records
product configuration not traceable from records
changes to config not controlled through formal process
requirements.applicability: Required when configuration management is in scope (typically all aerospace hardware manufacturers).

requirements.title: Control of Documented Information — Aerospace Addition
requirements.intent: External-origin documented information (customer drawings, specifications, regulatory documents, industry standards) is identified, controlled, and current.
expected_evidence: process for receiving and distributing customer-revised drawings
failure_modes: no process for receiving drawing revisions

requirements.title: Operational Planning and Control
requirements.intent: Organization plans, implements, and controls processes for product/service delivery. Plans include criteria, resources, controls, monitoring, and documented information requirements.
failure_modes: acceptance criteria not defined at operation level
controls stated as "per drawing" without verifying drawing callouts

requirements.title: Operational Planning (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Planning addresses customer-specific requirements, special requirements, critical items, and applicable statutory/regulatory requirements. Plans are reviewed with changes and communicated to affected functions.
expected_evidence: Quality plan or equivalent addressing all customer-specific requirements
failure_modes: Generic quality plans with no customer-specific content
planning not updated when requirements change

requirements.title: Configuration Management (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Formal configuration management process controls the identification, documentation, control, status accounting, and audit of product configuration throughout the lifecycle.
requirements.applicability: All organizations — level of rigor scales with contract requirements, but process must exist.

requirements.title: Product Safety (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Organization addresses product safety requirements relevant to its products and processes. Includes identification of safety-critical items, applicable regulatory requirements, and implementation of controls.
expected_evidence: identification of safety-critical items (SCIs) or critical safety items (CSIs)
linkage to regulatory requirements (e.g., FAA airworthiness data)
failure_modes: Product safety not addressed in QMS documentation
regulatory requirements for safety not referenced
safety culture not demonstrated in documentation
requirements.applicability: All organizations — required regardless of whether all products are safety-critical; the process for identifying and controlling safety items must exist.

requirements.title: Prevention of Counterfeit Parts (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Organization has documented process to prevent counterfeit or suspect unapproved parts from entering the supply chain and products. Includes procurement controls, verification, and reporting.
failure_modes: "we only buy from authorized distributors" is stated but not controlled
requirements.applicability: All organizations — applies to any organization that procures parts, materials, or assemblies.

requirements.title: Customer Communication
requirements.intent: Processes for communicating with customers include product/service information, inquiries, contracts, changes, customer property, and customer feedback including complaints.
failure_modes: no defined process for handling contract changes

requirements.title: Customer Communication (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Customer communication processes include specific aerospace requirements: escape notification, customer complaint response, and product field notifications when nonconformances affect already-delivered products.
expected_evidence: documented customer notification process for escapes
failure_modes: no process for tracking escape notifications to closure

requirements.title: Determining Requirements for Products and Services
requirements.intent: Organization determines statutory, regulatory, and customer requirements for products/services, including those not explicitly stated but necessary for intended use.
failure_modes: implied requirements (fitness for purpose) not addressed

requirements.title: Determining Requirements (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Requirements determination includes identification of applicable statutory/regulatory requirements including airworthiness requirements, customer-delegated inspection requirements, and applicable design data.
expected_evidence: applicable specifications identified in contract review
failure_modes: Airworthiness requirements not identified during contract review

requirements.title: Review of Requirements for Products and Services
requirements.intent: Organization reviews requirements before committing to supply. Resolves differences. Retains documented information on results of review and new requirements.

requirements.title: Review of Requirements (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Contract review ensures applicable statutory/regulatory requirements are identified, conflicts resolved, and organization has capability to meet requirements before acceptance.
expected_evidence: Capability review in contract review process
records showing regulatory requirements identified per contract
failure_modes: Capability assessment not part of contract review
no regulatory check at contract review

requirements.title: Design and Development
requirements.intent: Design and development process is planned and controlled. Inputs, outputs, reviews, verification, validation, and changes are all controlled. (Full clause — 8.3.1 through 8.3.6.)
failure_modes: design outputs not controlled through document control
requirements.applicability: Required unless a documented design exclusion is justified per 4.3.1. If claimed exclusion, verify.

requirements.title: Design and Development Planning (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Design planning addresses customer requirements, regulatory requirements, technical risk, lessons learned from similar designs, and identification of key characteristics.
expected_evidence: regulatory requirement identification in design plan
failure_modes: Generic design plans with no KC identification
regulatory requirements not addressed in design planning

requirements.title: Design Inputs (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Design inputs include statutory/regulatory requirements, applicable airworthiness requirements, product safety requirements, and results of risk management.
expected_evidence: Design input document listing regulatory requirements
risk management results as design inputs
airworthiness data identified as design inputs
failure_modes: Regulatory/airworthiness requirements not captured as formal design inputs
risk management outputs not feeding design inputs
safety requirements not in design inputs

requirements.title: Design Controls (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Design controls include design reviews at appropriate stages, use of alternative calculation methods, and testing when design cannot be verified by analysis.
failure_modes: Design reviews not at defined gates
tests substituted for verification without justification

requirements.title: Design Outputs (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Design outputs include identification of key characteristics, product safety requirements, and applicable statutory/regulatory requirements flowed to manufacturing and inspection.
failure_modes: KCs identified in design but not flowed to manufacturing documents
safety requirements not on manufacturing records

requirements.title: Design Changes (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Design changes are controlled, reviewed for airworthiness impact, customer approval obtained when required, and regulatory notification made when required.
failure_modes: informal changes to approved design data

requirements.title: Control of Externally Provided Processes, Products, and Services
requirements.intent: External providers are selected, evaluated, and controlled. Requirements flowed down. Performance monitored.

requirements.title: Supplier Control (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Organization controls externally provided processes to ensure they meet requirements. Applies to sub-tier suppliers including distributors and special process providers. Controls proportionate to risk.
expected_evidence: different control levels per risk tier
failure_modes: All suppliers treated identically regardless of risk
distributors not subject to counterfeit parts controls
special process suppliers not required to be qualified to applicable standards

requirements.title: Use of Customer-Directed Sources (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: When customers mandate specific external providers, the organization flows down requirements to those providers and maintains oversight appropriate to risk.
expected_evidence: oversight proportionate to risk even for mandated sources
failure_modes: Mandated sources used with no flow-down
assumption that customer selection equals control

requirements.title: Type and Extent of Control (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Organization defines type and extent of control applied to external providers, based on risk and capability. Controls include source inspection, certificates of conformance, first article, and sub-tier supplier controls.
failure_modes: no source inspection for high-risk suppliers

requirements.title: Verification of Conformity (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Organization verifies externally provided products/services meet requirements before acceptance. Includes inspection, testing, or review of objective evidence.
expected_evidence: first article inspection results from suppliers
failure_modes: products moved to stock before inspection complete

requirements.title: Information for External Providers
requirements.intent: Organization communicates requirements to external providers including product/process/equipment requirements, qualification requirements, QMS requirements, and customer flow-down requirements.
expected_evidence: flow-down of applicable customer and regulatory requirements
failure_modes: Purchase orders reference drawings only without specifying quality requirements
regulatory requirements not on purchase documents

requirements.title: Information for External Providers (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Flow-down includes: applicable design data revision, applicable regulatory/airworthiness requirements, applicable special process requirements, record retention requirements, customer notification requirements, and right of access for customer and regulatory authorities.
expected_evidence: Purchase orders or SQRs specifying design data revision
failure_modes: Design data revision not on PO

requirements.title: Control of Production and Service Provision
requirements.intent: Production and service provision is controlled under defined conditions including documented information, monitoring, measurement, infrastructure, and competent personnel.
expected_evidence: acceptance criteria available at point of use
monitoring and measurement at defined points
failure_modes: Work instructions not at point of use
acceptance criteria not available to operators
informal verbal instructions substituting for documented requirements

requirements.title: Control of Production (Aerospace Addition — FAI, KC, Special Requirements)
requirements.intent: Production controls include: documentation of product/process characteristics, first article inspection (FAI) when required, key characteristic controls, approval of production processes and equipment, control of work performed outside normal facilities.
expected_evidence: FAI procedure and records (per AS9102 or equivalent)
failure_modes: KCs identified but no control plan
KCs monitored by 100% inspection with no alternate method
no approved process or tooling list
requirements.applicability: FAI: when manufacturing to customer-controlled designs. KC: when KCs identified. Must be addressed regardless.

requirements.title: Control of Special Processes (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Special processes (those where output cannot be fully verified by subsequent inspection) are controlled by: qualified processes, qualified equipment, qualified personnel, and monitoring of process parameters.
expected_evidence: List of special processes in scope
qualification status of each (e.g., Nadcap, customer approval)
approved process specifications referenced in work instructions
failure_modes: Special processes not identified as such
no Nadcap or customer approval where required
personnel not qualified per applicable standard
WIs reference process specs by name without revision control
requirements.applicability: Required when ANY special processes are performed or outsourced.

requirements.title: Control of Production Equipment, Tools, and NC Software (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Production equipment, tooling, and numerically controlled (NC) software used in production are identified, controlled, and maintained. Includes tool qualification and software verification.
requirements.applicability: All organizations with production tooling or NC equipment.

requirements.title: Identification and Traceability
requirements.intent: Product is identified throughout production and delivery. Traceability maintained to the extent required. Inspection and test status maintained throughout.

requirements.title: Identification and Traceability (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Traceability maintained through the full supply chain when required. Specific records capture: lot/batch, heat/melt, serial number, and critical characteristics as applicable. Customer-imposed traceability requirements flowed down from contracts.
expected_evidence: Customer traceability requirements captured in contract review
raw material traceability to mill cert
failure_modes: Customer traceability requirements not identified or implemented
raw material certificates not linked to parts produced
no lot-to-serial link for critical items
requirements.applicability: All organizations — level of traceability scales with customer/regulatory requirements.

requirements.title: Property Belonging to Customers or External Providers
requirements.intent: Customer and external provider property is identified, verified, protected, and safeguarded. Lost, damaged, or unsuitable property is reported to the owner.
requirements.applicability: All organizations receiving customer or supplier property. Required when customer-furnished tooling, equipment, or material is used.

requirements.title: Preservation
requirements.intent: Product is preserved during production and delivery to maintain conformity. Includes identification, handling, packaging, storage, transmission/transport, and protection.

requirements.title: Post-Delivery Activities
requirements.intent: Organization determines extent of post-delivery activities required by customer, statutory/regulatory requirements, or organization itself. Includes warranty, maintenance, recycling.
failure_modes: in-service issues not fed back to QMS
requirements.applicability: All organizations — extent varies by product type and customer requirements.

requirements.title: Control of Changes
requirements.intent: Changes to production/service provision are reviewed and controlled to ensure continuing conformity. Persons authorizing changes are identified.

requirements.title: Control of Changes (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Production process changes are evaluated for impact on product conformity, customer notification requirements, and regulatory notification requirements. Changes to approved processes require re-approval.
failure_modes: regulatory authority not notified when required
approved process changes implemented without re-approval
requirements.applicability: All organizations — critical for FAA/EASA approved organizations.

requirements.title: Release of Products and Services
requirements.intent: Product is not released until all planned arrangements are satisfactorily completed. Authorized personnel documented. Records of release retained.
expected_evidence: records showing all requirements met before release

requirements.title: Release (Aerospace Addition — Authorized Release)
requirements.intent: Release documentation (Certificate of Conformance, FAA Form 8130-3, EASA Form 1, or equivalent) includes all required data elements: part number, description, quantity, conformance statement, authorizing signature, date, and applicable regulatory references.
expected_evidence: Signed CoC or authorized release document
references to applicable standards, drawings, and regulatory basis
authorized signatory with appropriate delegation of authority
failure_modes: no reference to applicable regulatory basis
generic conformance statements not linked to specific requirements
requirements.applicability: All organizations — specific form depends on regulatory context.

requirements.title: Inspection Documentation (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Inspection/test documentation is maintained that demonstrates conformity to acceptance criteria at each inspection point. Includes first article, in-process, and final inspection records.
expected_evidence: Inspection records at each defined point
failure_modes: results recorded without reference to acceptance criteria

requirements.title: Documentation of Product Release (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Records of product release include evidence of conformity to applicable requirements and traceability to the authorizing person.
expected_evidence: Complete release package linked to product (serial/lot)
failure_modes: traceability broken between inspection records and released product
conformance statement not linked to specific requirements met

requirements.title: Documentation for Authorized Release Organizations (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: When organization is authorized by a regulatory body (FAA, EASA, etc.) to issue authorized release documents, the process ensures compliance with the regulatory authorization scope and conditions.
expected_evidence: authorized signatory lists with current authority
failure_modes: records do not meet regulatory format requirements
requirements.applicability: Organizations with regulatory release authorization (FAA, EASA, CAAC, etc.).

requirements.title: Statutory/Regulatory Release Requirements (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Release activities comply with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements. Regulatory requirements do not yield to internal preferences.
failure_modes: Internal release process conflicts with regulatory requirements
regulatory requirements not checked at release

requirements.title: Customer Delegated Inspection (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: When customers delegate inspection authority to the organization, the delegation is formally accepted, scope is understood, and activities are performed per delegation terms.
requirements.applicability: When customers formally delegate inspection authority.

requirements.title: Control of Nonconforming Outputs
requirements.intent: Nonconforming products/processes are identified, controlled, and dispositioned. Prevent unintended use or delivery.
expected_evidence: disposition records (use as is, rework, scrap, return)

requirements.title: Control of Nonconforming Outputs (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: NCR process includes: documentation of nonconformance, containment, root cause analysis triggers, disposition authorization (with approvals), customer notification for escapes, regulatory notification when required, and concession/waiver request process.
expected_evidence: NCR form with all required fields

requirements.title: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis, and Evaluation
requirements.intent: Organization determines what to monitor, how, when, and when results are analyzed and evaluated. Includes customer satisfaction, process performance, and product conformity.
failure_modes: metrics tracked but not analyzed for trends

requirements.title: Monitoring (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Monitoring program includes: on-time delivery, quality escapes, supplier performance, internal audit results, and corrective action cycle time. Data is used to drive continual improvement.
expected_evidence: KPI set addressing all required areas
management review input records with trend data
failure_modes: KPIs exist but not all required areas covered
performance data collected but not used
management review does not review trend data

requirements.title: Analysis and Evaluation (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Analysis results are used to evaluate QMS effectiveness, identify improvement opportunities, and support management review. Analysis includes statistical methods where appropriate.
failure_modes: Data collected but no analysis performed
no statistical methods applied where appropriate
analysis results not fed into improvement activities
management review receives raw data not analysis

requirements.title: Internal Audit
requirements.intent: Internal audit program covers the full QMS, is planned based on risk, uses competent auditors independent of audited area, reports results to management, and drives corrective action.
failure_modes: audit scope does not cover all QMS elements

requirements.title: Internal Audit (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Audit program considers: process complexity, risk, previous audit results, customer feedback, and applicable regulatory requirements. Auditor qualification level commensurate with audit complexity.
expected_evidence: previous audit results used in scheduling
regulatory requirements included in audit scope
failure_modes: Audit schedule based on calendar only (not risk)
regulatory requirements not included in audit scope

requirements.title: Management Review
requirements.intent: Top management reviews QMS at planned intervals to ensure continuing suitability, adequacy, effectiveness, and alignment with strategic direction. Includes all required inputs and produces documented outputs.
expected_evidence: review records with all required inputs addressed
action items with owners and timelines

requirements.title: Management Review (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Management review inputs include: status of quality objectives, feedback from external parties including regulatory bodies, and results of risk management.
expected_evidence: Management review agenda addressing all inputs including regulatory feedback
risk management results as agenda input
failure_modes: Regulatory body feedback not included as input

requirements.title: Management Review Outputs (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Management review outputs address: QMS effectiveness decisions, continual improvement decisions, resources needed, and actions on risks and opportunities.
failure_modes: Review minutes with no actionable outputs

requirements.title: Nonconformity and Corrective Action
requirements.intent: Nonconformities are reacted to, root causes determined, corrective actions implemented, and effectiveness verified. Systematic process applied.
failure_modes: CARs closed without root cause analysis
management not aware of systemic issues

requirements.title: Corrective Action (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Corrective action process includes: timely response, containment, root cause analysis (using appropriate tools), action implementation, effectiveness verification, flow to similar processes and products, and management review of systemic findings.
expected_evidence: CAR records showing: containment, root cause (using systematic method — 5-Why, 8D, Fishbone, etc.), corrective actions, implementation evidence, effectiveness verification, applicability to similar processes, management review of trends
failure_modes: root cause is proximate not systemic
systemic findings not escalated to management review

requirements.title: CAR Requirements (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: CARs for significant nonconformities include timelines for completion, escalation triggers for overdue actions, and verification that actions were effective before closure.
failure_modes: CARs closed by originator without independent verification
systemic CARs closed without verifying recurrence prevention

requirements.title: Continual Improvement
requirements.intent: Organization continually improves QMS suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness. Uses analysis of data, audit results, lessons learned, and management review to drive improvement.
expected_evidence: continual improvement linkage to management review
failure_modes: Continual improvement mentioned but no evidence of systematic improvement activities
lessons learned not integrated into QMS

requirements.title: Scope and Regulatory Authorization Alignment
requirements.intent: The QMS scope must align precisely with the organization's regulatory authorization (repair station certificate, Part-145 approval, etc.). The QMS cannot authorize activities beyond what the regulatory certificate permits, and must address all authorized activities.
expected_evidence: Scope statement referencing regulatory certificate number and issuing authority
capability list or ratings list aligned to scope
exclusions documented where QMS scope is narrower than regulatory authorization
failure_modes: QMS scope states broad capability not reflected in regulatory authorization
regulatory limitations not referenced in scope
capability list not cross-referenced to scope
scope not updated when regulatory authorization changes
requirements.applicability: All AS9110C organizations. No exclusion permitted.

requirements.title: Maintenance Tooling and Equipment
requirements.intent: Tooling and equipment used in maintenance are identified, controlled, calibrated (where applicable), and maintained. Special tooling required by manufacturer technical data is available and approved.
expected_evidence: special tooling identification and approval records
failure_modes: calibrated tools mixed with uncalibrated tools
tools used beyond calibration due date

requirements.title: Human Factors in Maintenance (Aerospace Addition)
requirements.intent: Organization implements a formal human factors program addressing the conditions and factors that affect human performance in maintenance. Program includes error reporting, error investigation, and feedback to prevent recurrence.
expected_evidence: Human factors policy or program document
PEAR model or equivalent framework referenced
maintenance error reporting system (confidential where possible)
feedback loop to training, procedures, and risk management
failure_modes: No human factors program — only general safety awareness
error reporting is punitive rather than confidential
no investigation process for maintenance errors
human factors limited to training without system-level controls
no feedback from error reports to procedural improvements
requirements.applicability: All organizations — one of the most consistently audited areas in AS9110C.

requirements.title: Calibration Traceability in Maintenance Context
requirements.intent: Calibration of measurement and test equipment used in maintenance is traceable to national or international standards. Out-of-tolerance response includes assessment of maintenance tasks performed with the equipment.
expected_evidence: customer notification process when OOT equipment affected previously released work
failure_modes: OOT equipment discovered with no task impact review
no customer notification when OOT equipment released aircraft
requirements.applicability: All organizations using calibrated measurement equipment.

requirements.title: Certifying Staff Qualification and Authorization
requirements.intent: Certifying staff are qualified, trained, and authorized in writing to issue maintenance releases within a defined scope. Authorization scope matches regulatory requirements. Currency and recurrency requirements defined and tracked.
expected_evidence: Written authorizations for all certifying staff with defined scope limits
list of currently authorized certifying staff maintained and current
failure_modes: authorization scope not defined (blanket "all aircraft" without specificity)
suspended authorizations not removed from active list
no assessment of initial qualification beyond training attendance
requirements.applicability: All organizations with certifying staff — Critical applicability.

requirements.title: Airworthiness Data Control (External Documents)
requirements.intent: Manufacturer technical data (AMM, CMM, SRM, IPC, AWM, service bulletins, ADs, etc.) is identified, controlled for currency, and available at point of use. Superseded data is removed. Currency is verified before task commencement.
expected_evidence: External document register for all airworthiness data
failure_modes: superseded manuals in use on hangar floor or in workshop
no currency check requirement before task
requirements.applicability: All organizations — one of the most consistently audited and failed areas in MRO audits.

requirements.title: Maintenance Planning and Control
requirements.intent: Maintenance activities are planned before commencement. Planning identifies applicable technical data, required resources, special tooling, competent personnel, and environmental conditions. Pre-task briefings and preparation are controlled.
expected_evidence: Work order or task card system
applicable technical data identified before task commencement
special task controls identified in planning phase
failure_modes: technical data not identified before task
resources (tools, parts, personnel) not confirmed before commencement
no pre-task check or briefing for complex tasks

requirements.title: Component Tracking and Traceability
requirements.intent: Components inducted for maintenance are uniquely identified and tracked throughout the maintenance process from induction to return to service or disposition. Traceability to maintenance records is maintained.
expected_evidence: records linking component to work performed
traceability from released component to maintenance record
failure_modes: components not uniquely identified at receipt
released component cannot be traced to maintenance records
multiple components pooled without individual tracking
requirements.applicability: Required for all component maintenance. Critical for life-limited parts.

requirements.title: Life-Limited Parts Control
requirements.intent: Life-limited parts (LLPs) are identified, tracked, and controlled throughout maintenance. Life status is verified at induction, updated per maintenance performed, and documented on release. Parts at or beyond their life limit are not returned to service.
expected_evidence: life status documentation (cycles, hours, calendar time)
LLP records retained for full service life
life status updated after maintenance affecting life
prohibition on return to service of life-expired parts
customer notification when LLP status discrepancy found
failure_modes: LLP status not verified at induction
LLP tracking not updated after maintenance
LLP released without current life status documentation
no process for handling parts with missing life records
requirements.applicability: Required when LLPs are within the organization's maintenance scope.

requirements.title: Prevention of Counterfeit and Unapproved Parts
requirements.intent: Organization prevents installation of counterfeit, bogus, or unapproved parts during maintenance. Controls include procurement channel management, receiving verification of airworthiness documentation, independent verification methods, and reporting.
expected_evidence: receiving inspection requiring airworthiness documentation (FAA 8130-3, EASA Form 1, or CoC from authorized source)
independent verification method for high-risk parts
suspect part quarantine and reporting process (GIDEP, EASI)
failure_modes: no verification of airworthiness documentation at receiving
suspect parts not quarantined or reported
no training for procurement and receiving personnel
requirements.applicability: All organizations procuring parts, materials, or consumables — Critical.

requirements.title: Product Safety in Maintenance
requirements.intent: Safety-critical maintenance tasks and safety-critical items are identified. Controls are implemented proportionate to safety risk. Personnel performing safety-critical tasks understand the safety implications.
expected_evidence: enhanced controls for safety-critical tasks (witness inspection, dual inspection, etc.)
regulatory requirements for safety-critical tasks addressed
failure_modes: no enhanced controls for safety-critical tasks
regulatory safety requirements not addressed in procedures
dual or independent inspection requirements not defined
requirements.applicability: All organizations — absence for organizations performing safety-critical maintenance is Critical.

requirements.title: Customer Requirements — Maintenance Context
requirements.intent: Requirements for maintenance are determined before work commencement, including: applicable technical data, customer-specific requirements, regulatory requirements, and any deferred defect limitations. Customer limitations or restrictions on maintenance scope are identified and communicated.
expected_evidence: customer-specific requirements captured at order intake
regulatory requirements identified per work order
failure_modes: deferred defects accepted without MEL/CDL review
regulatory requirements not identified per order

requirements.title: Subcontract Maintenance Control
requirements.intent: When maintenance tasks are subcontracted (subletting), the prime organization controls the subcontractor and remains responsible for airworthiness of the work. Subcontracted work is released back to the prime for final release to service.
expected_evidence: subcontractor qualification criteria (including regulatory authorization verification)
return of completed work with appropriate documentation
prime organization's release to service covers subcontracted work
failure_modes: subcontracted work released directly by subcontractor to customer without prime's review
right of access not in subcontract
requirements.applicability: Required when maintenance is sublet. Absence of approved subcontractor list is Critical.

requirements.title: Control of Maintenance Execution
requirements.intent: Maintenance tasks are performed under controlled conditions using: applicable technical data, approved tooling, qualified and authorized personnel, acceptance criteria, monitoring at defined points, and prevention of human error.
expected_evidence: Task cards or work orders referencing specific technical data revision
acceptance criteria at each task step
work performed only by qualified personnel
error-proofing applied to complex or error-prone steps
failure_modes: technical data referenced generically without revision
no acceptance criteria at task level
tasks completed and released without all required signatures
requirements.applicability: All organizations — core MRO control clause.

requirements.title: Human Factors in Maintenance Execution
requirements.intent: Maintenance task execution controls address human factors specifically. Maintenance error critical tasks (MECTs) are identified and receive enhanced controls. Shift handover controls prevent continuation errors. Fatigue and fitness-for-duty are addressed.
expected_evidence: enhanced controls for MECTs (witness inspection, independent re-inspection, etc.)
incomplete task identification in handover documentation
continuation authorization before resuming handed-over tasks
failure_modes: incomplete tasks not positively identified at handover
requirements.applicability: All organizations performing maintenance — one of the most frequently cited AS9110C clauses.

requirements.title: Special Processes in MRO Context
requirements.intent: Special processes used in maintenance (NDT, welding, composite repair, painting, plating, heat treatment) are performed by qualified processes with qualified equipment and qualified personnel. Process parameter monitoring is maintained.
expected_evidence: qualification status per process (Nadcap, customer approval, or regulatory acceptance)
qualified personnel records per applicable specification (NAS410 for NDT, etc.)
approved process specifications referenced in work instructions
sub-tier special process approvals where outsourced
failure_modes: work instructions do not reference approved process specifications
outsourced special processes to non-approved providers
requirements.applicability: Required when any special processes are performed or outsourced.

requirements.title: Identification and Traceability in Maintenance
requirements.intent: Components and assemblies are uniquely identified throughout maintenance. Inspection and test status is maintained at each stage. Traceability is maintained from induction through return to service. Life-limited parts are traceable through their complete maintenance history.
expected_evidence: complete maintenance record traceable to released component
LLP history traceable through all maintenance events
failure_modes: components reassembled without verifying they match the work order
released component not traceable to specific maintenance records

requirements.title: Customer Property in Maintenance
requirements.intent: Customer aircraft, engines, and components received for maintenance are verified at induction, identified, protected, and safeguarded throughout maintenance. Pre-existing damage is documented before work begins. Loss or damage during maintenance is reported.
expected_evidence: LLP and life status documentation verified at induction
failure_modes: customer components mixed with other customers' components
LLP status not verified at receipt
customer tooling not identified or protected
requirements.applicability: All organizations receiving customer aircraft, engines, or components.

requirements.title: Preservation of Components During Maintenance
requirements.intent: Components are preserved during maintenance to prevent damage, contamination, or degradation. Shelf-life of materials is controlled. ESD protection applied where required. Components stored appropriately between maintenance operations.
expected_evidence: shelf-life tracking for consumables and materials
failure_modes: open systems not protected from FOD

requirements.title: Return to Service and Authorized Release
requirements.intent: Maintenance release (return to service) is issued only by authorized certifying staff within their authorization scope. Release document contains all required data elements. Regulatory form requirements are met. Records support the release.
expected_evidence: authorized certifying staff list with current scope
release document template with all regulatory-required fields
records package linked to each release
regulatory form (8130-3, EASA Form 1, or equivalent) completed correctly
failure_modes: Release issued by person not on authorized list
requirements.applicability: All organizations — Critical applicability; unauthorized release is the most severe MRO finding.

requirements.title: Maintenance Release Documentation Requirements
requirements.intent: Release documents contain all elements required by applicable regulation and by AS9110C: description of work, technical data basis and revision, applicable regulatory reference, certifying staff identification and authorization number, date, and statement of conformity.
expected_evidence: Completed release documents from prior releases
record linkage to work orders and task cards
failure_modes: Missing required elements on release documents
statement of conformity absent or vague

requirements.title: Nonconforming Maintenance Outputs
requirements.intent: Nonconforming maintenance work (unsatisfactory conditions, out-of-tolerance findings, unairworthy conditions) is identified, controlled, and dispositioned before return to service. Customer and regulatory notification when escapes occur.
expected_evidence: NCR system adapted for maintenance context
quarantine and segregation of unserviceable components
disposition authority (repair, replace, return to customer unserviceable, scrap)
regulatory reporting where required (service difficulty reports, mandatory occurrence reports)
failure_modes: Nonconforming conditions identified but not formally documented
unserviceable components not tagged or segregated
dispositions made without engineering review where required

requirements.title: Maintenance Performance Monitoring
requirements.intent: Performance monitoring program includes MRO-specific metrics: on-time release, maintenance error rates, repeat maintenance, customer complaints, rework rates, and regulatory finding trends. Metrics fed to management review.
expected_evidence: regulatory finding integration in performance monitoring
failure_modes: Generic QMS KPIs only — no MRO-specific metrics
regulatory findings not integrated into performance monitoring

requirements.title: Internal Audit Scope in MRO Context
requirements.intent: Internal audit program covers both QMS and regulatory requirements. Audit scope includes hangar floor, workshop, and all authorized maintenance activities — not only administrative processes. Audit findings from regulatory authorities are integrated into the internal audit program.
expected_evidence: Audit program covering all maintenance activities and all applicable regulations
regulatory finding tracking integrated with internal audit
risk-based scheduling weighted toward airworthiness-critical processes
failure_modes: Audit covers QMS documents only — no hangar floor audit
regulatory requirements not in audit scope
audit schedule not weighted toward airworthiness-critical processes

requirements.title: Corrective Action — Maintenance Context
requirements.intent: Corrective action process addresses maintenance-specific failure modes. Root cause analysis accounts for human factors, systemic process weaknesses, and technical data issues — not only product or component deficiencies. Lessons learned feed back to task cards, training, and technical data.
expected_evidence: CAR records addressing maintenance-specific root causes
lessons learned linkage to task card updates, training updates, and technical data requests
management review of maintenance error trends
failure_modes: Root cause stops at "technician error" without systemic investigation
no feedback to task card design

requirements.title: Scope and Distribution Type Declaration
requirements.intent: Scope identifies whether the organization is an authorized distributor (OEM franchise) or independent distributor. This distinction drives the level of counterfeit risk controls required and is audited directly by CB auditors.
expected_evidence: Scope statement distinguishing authorized vs. independent status
reference to applicable franchise agreements or OEM authorization where applicable
distribution activities described with sufficient specificity
failure_modes: Scope does not identify distribution type
authorized status claimed without franchise documentation
independent distributor not acknowledging heightened counterfeit risk obligations

requirements.title: Product Knowledge as Organizational Knowledge
requirements.intent: The organization maintains knowledge of the products it distributes, including part number structures, interchangeability data, supersedure information, applicable specifications, and known obsolescence issues.
expected_evidence: Product knowledge repository or reference library
process for maintaining currency of product knowledge
failure_modes: personnel unable to identify interchangeable or superseded part numbers
no access to manufacturer technical data
product knowledge entirely dependent on a single individual

requirements.title: Flow-Down of Customer Requirements
requirements.intent: Customer requirements, including customer-specific quality requirements, regulatory requirements, and applicable flow-down requirements (Boeing D1-4426, Airbus AIPI, DCMA, etc.), are captured at order review and flowed through to purchasing, receiving, and shipping.
expected_evidence: Order review procedure capturing customer-specific requirements
mechanism to flow requirements to purchase orders
requirements traceable from customer order to purchasing activity
failure_modes: Customer-specific requirements not captured at order intake
requirements not flowed to purchase orders
"standard process" applied regardless of customer-specific needs

requirements.title: Prevention of Counterfeit and Suspect Unapproved Parts
requirements.intent: Organization implements a documented, layered counterfeit parts prevention program covering: source controls, receiving verification, independent verification for high-risk products, suspect part quarantine and disposition, GIDEP/ERAI reporting, and personnel training. Program is risk-proportionate and more stringent for independent distributors and high-demand/obsolete parts.
expected_evidence: approved source list with source type classification
receiving inspection requiring airworthiness documentation verification
independent verification method for high-risk parts (physical inspection, testing, third-party authentication)
training records for purchasing and receiving personnel
escalated controls for independent distribution activity
failure_modes: approved source list without risk classification
receiving inspection verifies packing slip only — no documentation or physical check
same controls for authorized and independent distribution channels
requirements.applicability: All organizations — one of the top 3 major findings in AS9120B audits.

requirements.title: Customer Requirements Including Flow-Down
requirements.intent: Requirements determination includes: customer-specified quality requirements, applicable airworthiness requirements, applicable customer-specific standards, and regulatory requirements applicable to the products being distributed.
expected_evidence: Requirements register or matrix per customer type
regulatory requirement identification for products distributed
customer-specific standard list per key customer
failure_modes: Only purchase order line items reviewed — quality requirements not captured
customer-specific standards (D1-4426, etc.) not identified or implemented

requirements.title: External Provider Control — Distribution Context
requirements.intent: External providers (sources from which product is procured) are evaluated and approved. Source type is classified (OEM, OEM-authorized distributor, independent distributor). Controls are risk-proportionate to source type and product criticality.
expected_evidence: Approved Source List (ASL) with source type classification
OEM authorization verification for authorized distributors
failure_modes: independent distributors not subject to heightened controls

requirements.title: Authorized Distributor Verification
requirements.intent: When procuring from authorized distributors, the organization verifies the source's authorized distributor status with the OEM or authorized manufacturer. Authorization verification is current and on file.
requirements.applicability: When procuring from claimed authorized distributors.

requirements.title: Independent Distributor Controls
requirements.intent: When procuring from independent distributors (no OEM franchise), enhanced controls are applied proportionate to the increased counterfeit and traceability risk. Controls include additional documentation requirements, physical inspection, and potentially third-party testing.
expected_evidence: enhanced receiving inspection procedure for independent distributor stock
additional documentation requirements (full unbroken chain from OEM)
restrictions on high-risk product categories from independent sources
failure_modes: Independent distributors treated identically to authorized distributors
no documentation chain requirements beyond basic CoC

requirements.title: Purchase Order Requirements
requirements.intent: Purchase orders communicate all applicable requirements to external providers including: specific part number and revision, quantity, applicable specifications, required documentation (CoC, 8130-3, test reports), traceability requirements, applicable customer flow-down requirements, and right of access.
expected_evidence: Purchase order template with required fields
mechanism to populate customer-specific requirements on PO
failure_modes: Purchase orders reference part number and quantity only

requirements.title: Receiving Inspection and Documentation Verification
requirements.intent: All incoming product is inspected at receiving for: physical condition, packaging integrity, quantity verification, and airworthiness documentation completeness and authenticity. Documentation verification includes CoC data elements, 8130-3 or equivalent, packing slip correlation, and counterfeit indicators check.
expected_evidence: Receiving inspection procedure with documented checklist
failure_modes: documentation verification is packing slip check only
requirements.applicability: All organizations — one of the most consistently audited AS9120B processes.

requirements.title: Traceability Through Distribution
requirements.intent: Traceability is maintained from the OEM source through all distribution activities (receiving, storage, lot splitting, repackaging, kitting, shipping) to the end customer. The documentation chain is unbroken. Each product unit or lot can be traced back to its original OEM release documentation.
expected_evidence: documentation retention linking product to source documentation
ability to trace any distributed part back to original CoC or 8130-3
failure_modes: Traceability breaks at any point in the distribution chain
inability to produce original source documentation for distributed product
products commingled across lots or sources
requirements.applicability: All organizations — the defining requirement of AS9120B.

requirements.title: Lot Splitting and Repackaging Traceability
requirements.intent: When lots are split or product is repackaged for distribution, traceability to the original OEM documentation is maintained and documented. New packaging references original lot and documentation. Customer is notified when documentation is reproduced.
expected_evidence: traceability records linking split lots to original lot and documentation
notification process when documentation is reproduced or reformatted
prohibition on creating new CoC without basis in original source documentation
failure_modes: new labels not referencing original source
organization issues its own CoC covering multiple source lots without traceability to each
commingling of different-source product in a single lot
requirements.applicability: When lot splitting or repackaging is performed.

requirements.title: Product Preservation in Distribution
requirements.intent: Product is stored, handled, and shipped in conditions that maintain conformity and preserve airworthiness documentation integrity. Shelf-life controlled materials are managed using FIFO or FEFO. Environmental controls prevent damage, contamination, or degradation.
expected_evidence: environmental condition controls (temperature, humidity, ESD, FOD)
customer notification when near-expiry product is shipped
failure_modes: ESD-sensitive parts stored without ESD protection
requirements.applicability: All organizations — shelf-life and ESD requirements are consistently audited.

requirements.title: Certificate of Conformance Issuance
requirements.intent: When the organization issues a Certificate of Conformance, the CoC is based on verified source documentation, contains all required data elements, is issued only by authorized personnel, and is traceable to the source documentation on which it is based. The organization never issues a CoC that makes claims not supported by verified source documentation.
expected_evidence: CoC template with required elements (part number, quantity, lot/batch, OEM source reference, applicable specifications, conformance statement, authorized signatory, date)
traceability from issued CoC to source documents
prohibition on issuing CoC without traceability basis
failure_modes: CoC issued without source documentation verification
CoC cannot be traced to source documentation
CoC makes conformance claims beyond what source documentation supports

requirements.title: Control of Nonconforming Product in Distribution
requirements.intent: Nonconforming product (damaged, discrepant documentation, suspect counterfeit, expired shelf-life) is identified, segregated, and dispositioned. Customer notification when nonconforming product may have shipped. Suspect counterfeit parts handled per special controls including quarantine, reporting, and prohibition on return to supply chain.
expected_evidence: NCR process adapted for distribution context
suspect counterfeit handling procedure including quarantine, reporting (GIDEP/ERAI), and prohibition on redistribution
failure_modes: discrepant product returned to stock without investigation
suspect counterfeit parts not quarantined or reported
returned customer product re-stocked without inspection

requirements.title: Customer Returns to Serviceable Stock
requirements.intent: Product returned by customers is not returned to serviceable inventory without re-inspection and re-verification of documentation integrity. Returned product is treated as of unknown status until verified.
expected_evidence: quarantine of returned product on receipt
re-inspection requirements before return to stock
disposition of product that cannot be verified
failure_modes: Returned product placed directly back into stock
no traceability of returned product through the return process
inability to identify returned product in subsequent sales

requirements.title: Distribution Performance Monitoring
requirements.intent: Performance monitoring includes distribution-specific metrics: on-time delivery, documentation error rate, customer complaints, counterfeit suspect incident rate, receiving rejection rate, and traceability discrepancy rate.

requirements.title: Corrective Action — Distribution Context
requirements.intent: Corrective action process addresses distribution-specific failure modes including traceability breaks, documentation errors, counterfeit suspect parts, and source control failures. Customer notification evaluated for all escapes.
expected_evidence: CAR records addressing distribution-specific root causes
supplier corrective action process for source-related nonconformances
failure_modes: CARs treat distribution findings as generic nonconformances
supplier not notified when source-related nonconformance found

requirements.title: Understanding the Organization and Its Context
requirements.intent: Organization systematically identifies internal and external issues that affect its ability to achieve intended QMS outcomes. This is the strategic foundation — auditors look for genuine analysis, not boilerplate.
expected_evidence: Context analysis (SWOT, PESTLE, or equivalent method)
evidence of monitoring and review (not just one-time exercise)
linkage to QMS scope and risk planning
failure_modes: Analysis is generic template text not specific to the organization
no linkage to QMS design or risk management

requirements.title: Understanding the Needs and Expectations of Interested Parties
requirements.intent: Organization identifies who has a stake in its QMS outputs and captures their relevant requirements. Drives completeness of QMS coverage beyond just "the customer."
expected_evidence: linkage to QMS processes and risk assessment
failure_modes: employees, regulators, certification bodies, suppliers, communities omitted

requirements.title: Determining the Scope of the QMS
requirements.intent: Scope is defined, documented, and maintained. All exclusions must be justified — only 8.3 (Design and Development) may be excluded and only when the organization genuinely has no design responsibility.
expected_evidence: Written scope statement specifying products/services, locations, and any exclusions with documented justification
failure_modes: 8.3 excluded when some design activity exists
scope not updated when business changes

requirements.title: QMS and Its Processes
requirements.intent: Organization determines, implements, maintains, and continually improves processes needed for the QMS. Processes are managed with defined inputs, outputs, sequence, interactions, criteria, responsibilities, and risks.
expected_evidence: risk and opportunity consideration per process
failure_modes: Process map is an org chart
processes described in isolation with no interfaces

requirements.title: Leadership and Commitment
requirements.intent: Top management demonstrates active accountability for QMS effectiveness — not just signing the policy. Includes ensuring alignment with strategic direction, integrating QMS requirements into business processes, and promoting customer focus.
expected_evidence: Management review records showing top management attendance and decisions
quality objectives approved by top management
customer focus demonstrated in management actions
failure_modes: Management review conducted without top management
objectives set by quality department without management endorsement
QMS treated as separate from business operations
management commitment limited to policy signature

requirements.title: Customer Focus
requirements.intent: Top management ensures customer requirements are determined and met, risks to conformity are addressed, and customer satisfaction is enhanced.
expected_evidence: evidence of top management review of customer feedback
customer focus in quality policy and objectives
failure_modes: Customer focus is a policy statement only
no active measurement of customer satisfaction
top management not involved in customer focus activities

requirements.title: Quality Policy
requirements.intent: Policy is appropriate to the organization's purpose and context, provides framework for objectives, commits to satisfying requirements and continual improvement, and is communicated, understood, and available.
failure_modes: generic text not specific to organization
doc_types: Quality Policy (standalone or within Quality Manual)

requirements.title: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
requirements.intent: Relevant roles, responsibilities, and authorities are assigned, communicated, and understood. Top management retains accountability but responsibility is distributed appropriately.
expected_evidence: deputy/backup roles for key quality functions
failure_modes: Org chart only — responsibilities not defined
all quality responsibilities assigned to "Quality" function with no specificity
QMS roles not linked to actual personnel

requirements.title: Actions to Address Risks and Opportunities
requirements.intent: Organization identifies risks and opportunities relevant to the QMS and plans proportionate actions. Risk-based thinking is systematic, documented, and effective — not reactive.
failure_modes: Risk assessment a one-time exercise never updated
only product risk considered (not QMS and process risk)
risk register exists but no actions taken
risk thinking limited to a paragraph in the Quality Manual
doc_types: Risk Management procedure (or equivalent section in QMS)
requirements.applicability: All organizations. This is a "shall" — documented approach required.

requirements.title: Quality Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them
requirements.intent: Quality objectives are established at relevant functions and levels, are measurable, consistent with the quality policy, and monitored. Plans to achieve them specify who, what, when, resources needed, and how evaluated.
expected_evidence: plans with responsible owners and timelines
failure_modes: objectives set once and never reviewed
objectives not deployed to relevant functions
objectives not consistent with policy commitments

requirements.title: Planning of Changes
requirements.intent: Changes to the QMS are planned and carried out in a controlled manner, considering purpose, potential consequences, integrity of QMS, resource availability, and allocation of responsibilities.
expected_evidence: Change control process for QMS changes
resource availability confirmed before change implementation

requirements.title: General Resources
requirements.intent: Organization determines and provides resources needed for QMS establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement, considering internal capabilities and external provider constraints.
expected_evidence: Resource planning linked to QMS objectives
failure_modes: No evidence of formal resource determination
no connection between QMS requirements and resource planning

requirements.title: People
requirements.intent: Adequate, competent personnel are provided for effective QMS implementation and operation of processes.
expected_evidence: personnel records linked to QMS roles
failure_modes: No evidence of personnel planning linked to QMS needs
staffing decisions disconnected from QMS requirements

requirements.title: Infrastructure
requirements.intent: Infrastructure (buildings, utilities, equipment, transportation, IT) is determined, provided, and maintained to achieve product and service conformity.
failure_modes: No infrastructure list linked to QMS
IT systems used for QMS not addressed
equipment used for product conformity not controlled

requirements.title: Process Environment
requirements.intent: Work environment is controlled to the extent necessary to achieve conformity. Includes physical, social, and psychological factors (cleanliness, temperature, lighting, stress, recognition).
expected_evidence: work environment factors considered in process planning
failure_modes: temperature/humidity controls undocumented where product is affected
ESD controls absent for electronic products
environmental factors not linked to product conformity
requirements.applicability: All organizations — extent proportionate to impact on product/service conformity.

requirements.title: Monitoring and Measuring Resources
requirements.intent: Resources used for monitoring and measurement are suitable, maintained, and retained in a state that demonstrates fitness for purpose. Where traceability is required, calibration is traceable.
expected_evidence: traceability to national/international standards where required
failure_modes: equipment used beyond calibration due date
requirements.applicability: All organizations with measurement equipment used to verify conformity.

requirements.title: Measurement Traceability
requirements.intent: Where measurement traceability is a requirement (or is considered essential), measurement equipment is calibrated/verified at specified intervals against measurement standards traceable to national or international measurement standards.
expected_evidence: Calibration certificates referencing traceability chain (e.g., NIST)
failure_modes: internal standards not calibrated against traceable references
requirements.applicability: Where traceability is a requirement or essential for confidence in measurement results.

requirements.title: Organizational Knowledge
requirements.intent: Organization determines knowledge needed for processes and conformity, maintains it, makes it available, and considers future needs. Addresses lessons learned and how knowledge is captured when personnel depart.
expected_evidence: knowledge transfer process for critical roles
failure_modes: expert knowledge at risk of loss when personnel depart
no process for acquiring needed new knowledge

requirements.title: Competence
requirements.intent: Personnel affecting quality performance are competent based on education, training, or experience. Where gaps exist, action is taken and effectiveness evaluated.
expected_evidence: training effectiveness evaluation (not just attendance records)
failure_modes: Attendance records substituted for competency records
competency matrix not linked to job roles or QMS processes

requirements.title: Awareness
requirements.intent: Persons doing work affecting QMS performance are aware of the quality policy, relevant objectives, their contribution to QMS effectiveness, and implications of nonconformity.
expected_evidence: ability of personnel to demonstrate awareness (interview-verified)
failure_modes: personnel cannot articulate policy or objectives
onboarding does not include QMS awareness

requirements.title: Communication
requirements.intent: Organization determines relevant internal and external communication — what to communicate, when, with whom, how, and who communicates.
expected_evidence: communication triggers defined for key events
failure_modes: no defined triggers for required communications
QMS changes not communicated to affected personnel

requirements.title: Documented Information
requirements.intent: Required documented information (both documents and records) is created, controlled, and maintained. Appropriate format, media, distribution, access, retrieval, use, storage, protection, and retention/disposal.
expected_evidence: master document list or equivalent control

requirements.title: Operational Planning and Control
requirements.intent: Organization plans, implements, controls, and maintains processes needed for product/service realization. Criteria for processes, acceptance of products/services, and control of planned changes — including review of unintended changes.
failure_modes: acceptance criteria not defined at point of use
controls stated by reference only without verification they are implemented

requirements.title: Customer Communication
requirements.intent: Communication with customers covers: product/service information, inquiries, contracts and orders (including changes), customer feedback (including complaints), customer property handling, and contingency requirements.
failure_modes: no defined response process for customer feedback

requirements.title: Determining Requirements for Products and Services
requirements.intent: Organization determines requirements for products/services, including statutory and regulatory requirements and those considered necessary by the organization but not stated by the customer.
failure_modes: "standard product" treated as having no requirements

requirements.title: Review of Requirements for Products and Services
requirements.intent: Before committing to supply, organization reviews requirements to ensure they are defined, any conflicts are resolved, and the organization can meet them. Changes to requirements communicated to all affected functions.
failure_modes: affected functions not informed of requirement changes

requirements.title: Design and Development (When Applicable)
requirements.intent: Design and development is planned and controlled across all phases: planning (8.3.2), inputs (8.3.3), controls (8.3.4), outputs (8.3.5), and changes (8.3.6). Outputs are verified against inputs and validated before release.
expected_evidence: design change records (all controlled through document control)
failure_modes: design outputs not linked to controlled documents
requirements.applicability: Required unless organization genuinely has no design responsibility and exclusion is documented per 4.3.

requirements.title: Control of Externally Provided Processes, Products, and Services
requirements.intent: External providers are evaluated, selected, monitored, and re-evaluated. Requirements are communicated. Controls are proportionate to risk and impact on conformity.
failure_modes: evaluation criteria undefined ("we know them well")
requirements communicated verbally not in writing
outsourced processes treated as fully delegated
requirements.applicability: All organizations with external providers, including outsourced QMS processes.

requirements.title: General External Provider Controls
requirements.intent: Organization ensures externally provided processes, products, and services conform to requirements. Type and extent of control is risk-based.
expected_evidence: different control levels per risk tier
failure_modes: All suppliers treated identically regardless of risk
high-risk external providers with minimal controls
outsourced processes treated as fully exempt from QMS oversight

requirements.title: Type and Extent of Control
requirements.intent: Organization controls externally provided processes within QMS. Controls prevent delivery of nonconforming items. Verification activities defined.
failure_modes: no verification of conformity before acceptance

requirements.title: Information for External Providers
requirements.intent: Organization communicates requirements to external providers including: processes/products/services to be provided, approval requirements, competence requirements, QMS requirements, and monitoring/verification activities.

requirements.title: Control of Production and Service Provision
requirements.intent: Production/service provision is carried out under controlled conditions including: documented information specifying characteristics, monitoring/measuring activities, use of suitable infrastructure, appointment of competent persons, implementation of monitoring actions, and activities to prevent human error.
expected_evidence: acceptance criteria at point of use
failure_modes: Work instructions absent or inaccessible at point of use
