informal verbal instructions substitute for documents

requirements.title: Identification and Traceability
requirements.intent: Outputs are identified throughout production/service provision. Inspection and test status is identified. Traceability is controlled to the extent required.
failure_modes: inspection status ambiguous at point of use
nonconforming product not segregated or marked
requirements.applicability: All organizations — extent scales with requirements and risk.

requirements.title: Property Belonging to Customers or External Providers
requirements.intent: Property belonging to customers or external providers is identified, verified, protected, and safeguarded. If lost, damaged, or unsuitable, reported to owner.
requirements.applicability: When organization receives/uses property belonging to customers or external providers.

requirements.title: Preservation
requirements.intent: Outputs are preserved during production and delivery to maintain conformity, including identification, handling, contamination control, packaging, storage, transmission, and protection.
failure_modes: preservation requirements not defined for fragile or sensitive products

requirements.title: Post-Delivery Activities
requirements.intent: Organization meets requirements for post-delivery activities to the extent required by: statutory/regulatory requirements, customer requirements, nature of products/services, and organization's own determinations.
expected_evidence: Post-delivery requirements identified in contract review
failure_modes: in-service failures not fed back to QMS improvement
requirements.applicability: All organizations — extent varies by product/service type.

requirements.title: Control of Changes
requirements.intent: Organization reviews and controls changes to production/service provision to ensure continuing conformity. Authorized persons documented. Records of results of review, authorization, and necessary actions retained.

requirements.title: Release of Products and Services
requirements.intent: Products and services are not released until planned arrangements are completed satisfactorily (unless approved by relevant authority and where applicable by customer). Records retained identifying: conformity criteria, conforming evidence, traceability to authorizing person, and date.
expected_evidence: records showing all planned requirements met
failure_modes: Release without completing all planned inspections
records not traceable to specific product

requirements.title: Control of Nonconforming Outputs
requirements.intent: Outputs that do not conform to requirements are identified and controlled to prevent unintended use or delivery. Disposition is controlled and authorized. Corrective action triggered when appropriate.

requirements.title: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis, and Evaluation
requirements.intent: Organization determines what to monitor and measure, methods for valid results, when to monitor and analyze, when to report. Evaluates QMS performance and effectiveness.
expected_evidence: management review inputs with analyzed data

requirements.title: Customer Satisfaction
requirements.intent: Organization monitors customers' perceptions of the degree to which their needs and expectations have been fulfilled. Methods defined and used.
failure_modes: surveys sent but results not analyzed
customer satisfaction data not used for improvement

requirements.title: Analysis and Evaluation
requirements.intent: Organization analyzes and evaluates data from monitoring and measurement to assess: conformity of products/services, customer satisfaction, QMS performance and effectiveness, planning effectiveness, risk action effectiveness, external provider performance, and improvement needs.
failure_modes: raw data reported to management without analysis
analysis not covering all required areas
no improvement opportunities identified from analysis

requirements.title: Internal Audit
requirements.intent: Internal audit program covers all QMS processes and requirements at planned intervals, using competent and objective auditors, and reporting results to management for corrective action.
failure_modes: Full QMS not covered in audit cycle

requirements.title: Management Review
requirements.intent: Top management reviews QMS at planned intervals to ensure continuing suitability, adequacy, effectiveness, and alignment with strategic direction. All required inputs reviewed; outputs include decisions and action items.
expected_evidence: records with all required inputs addressed
action items with owners and timelines
failure_modes: Required inputs not all addressed (missing any one is a finding)
outputs are minutes with no actionable commitments

requirements.title: General Improvement
requirements.intent: Organization determines and selects opportunities for improvement and implements actions to meet customer requirements and enhance satisfaction. Includes product/service improvement, correcting/preventing undesired effects, and improving QMS performance.
expected_evidence: linkage between analysis results and improvement actions
failure_modes: analysis results not converting to improvement actions

requirements.title: Nonconformity and Corrective Action
requirements.intent: When nonconformity occurs: react and control; evaluate root cause; implement corrective action; verify effectiveness; update risks and lessons learned; change QMS if needed. Process is systematic and documented.
expected_evidence: CAR records with all required elements (reaction, containment, root cause, actions, effectiveness verification)
failure_modes: CARs closed without root cause analysis
root cause is proximate not systemic
actions not verified for effectiveness before closure
systemic issues not escalated to management
QMS not updated based on lessons learned

requirements.title: Continual Improvement
requirements.intent: Organization continually improves suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the QMS. Uses results of analysis, management review outputs, lessons learned, and improvement initiatives.
expected_evidence: lessons learned feeding back into QMS
failure_modes: "Continual improvement" stated but no evidence of systematic improvement activities
management review recommends improvements but no follow-through

requirements.title: General Requirements
requirements.intent: Organization establishes, documents, implements, maintains, and continually improves the QMS in accordance with ISO 13485:2016 AND applicable regulatory requirements. Processes are identified, sequenced, monitored, and managed. Outsourced processes are controlled.
expected_evidence: monitoring and measurement of QMS processes
applicable regulatory requirements identified for each market
failure_modes: QMS established for ISO 13485 but applicable regulatory requirements not identified

requirements.title: Documentation Requirements — General
requirements.intent: QMS documentation includes: quality policy, quality manual, required procedures and records, and documents needed to ensure effective planning, operation, and control of processes. Documentation is appropriate to the regulatory requirements of the jurisdictions in which the organization operates.
expected_evidence: Complete documentation set including all required procedures
documents appropriate to jurisdiction-specific regulatory requirements
failure_modes: documentation not addressing all applicable regulatory requirements

requirements.title: Quality Manual
requirements.intent: Quality manual is required (not optional). Includes: scope with justification for any exclusions (only 7.3 is excludable if no design responsibility), documented procedures or references, and description of interactions between QMS processes.
expected_evidence: justification for any exclusions (7.3 only, regulatory limitations must be documented for other exclusions)
failure_modes: exclusions claimed beyond 7.3 without regulatory justification
quality manual not maintained to current QMS state
requirements.applicability: All organizations — quality manual is mandatory in ISO 13485; this differs from ISO 9001:2015.

requirements.title: Medical Device File
requirements.intent: For each medical device or device family, the organization maintains or specifies the location of a medical device file containing documents and records demonstrating conformity to requirements and regulatory requirements. File must be product/family specific.
expected_evidence: Medical device file index or structure per product

file contains or references: device description, specifications, design outputs, labeling, manufacturing information, risk management summary, clinical evaluation/performance summary, regulatory submissions/approvals
failure_modes: file does not reference all required content
regulatory submission records not linked to file
requirements.applicability: All organizations — one of the most frequently audited ISO 13485-specific requirements.

requirements.title: Control of Documents
requirements.intent: Documents required by the QMS are controlled. Controls include: approval, review, update, reissue, identification of current revision, availability at point of use, readability, external document identification and control, and prevention of obsolete document use.
failure_modes: Obsolete documents in use at point of use

requirements.title: Control of Records
requirements.intent: Records required by ISO 13485 and applicable regulatory requirements are established and maintained. Controls include: identification, storage, protection, retrieval, retention time, and disposal. Retention periods must meet or exceed regulatory requirements (often 2 years from manufacturing date, or the lifetime of the device plus 2 years — whichever is longer).
expected_evidence: Record retention schedule with regulatory-required periods
records readable for full retention period
failure_modes: Retention periods not meeting regulatory minimums

requirements.title: Management Commitment
requirements.intent: Top management demonstrates commitment to developing and implementing the QMS and maintaining its effectiveness. Commits to meeting customer requirements AND applicable regulatory requirements. Establishes quality policy and objectives. Conducts management reviews. Ensures availability of resources.
expected_evidence: Quality policy signed by top management
management review attendance by top management
evidence of top management involvement in QMS decisions
regulatory requirements acknowledged at management level
failure_modes: QMS managed entirely below top management level
regulatory requirements not acknowledged in management documentation
resource allocation not connected to QMS needs

requirements.title: Customer Focus
requirements.intent: Top management ensures customer requirements and applicable regulatory requirements are determined and met with aim of enhancing customer satisfaction (where applicable) and meeting regulatory requirements. Note: ISO 13485 balances customer satisfaction with patient safety and regulatory compliance — regulatory requirements take precedence.
expected_evidence: process for identifying applicable regulatory requirements
customer and regulatory requirements feeding into QMS planning
failure_modes: no process to update requirements when regulations change

requirements.title: Quality Policy
requirements.intent: Quality policy is appropriate to the organization's purpose, includes commitment to compliance with requirements and applicable regulatory requirements, includes commitment to maintaining QMS effectiveness, provides framework for objectives, is communicated and understood, and is reviewed for suitability.
expected_evidence: Quality policy with compliance and regulatory commitments
failure_modes: policy does not reflect actual business scope

requirements.title: Planning
requirements.intent: Quality objectives are established at relevant functions and levels, are measurable, and are consistent with quality policy including commitment to compliance. QMS planning ensures objectives are met and integrity of QMS is maintained when changes are planned.
expected_evidence: change planning process maintaining QMS integrity
regulatory requirements reflected in objectives where applicable
failure_modes: changes to QMS made without maintaining integrity

requirements.title: Responsibility, Authority, and Communication
requirements.intent: Responsibilities and authorities are defined and communicated. Management representative appointed with specific ISO 13485 responsibilities including regulatory authority interface. Internal communication processes established for QMS effectiveness.
expected_evidence: internal communication records on QMS matters
failure_modes: no internal communication on QMS performance
quality concerns have no defined escalation path

requirements.title: Management Review
requirements.intent: Top management reviews QMS at planned intervals (typically annually minimum) to ensure continuing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness. All required inputs reviewed. Outputs include decisions and actions.
expected_evidence: Management review records with all required inputs
actions from prior review followed up
decisions documented with owners and timelines
failure_modes: regulatory changes not included as input

extra_fields.Required Outputs: Decisions and actions on: improvement of QMS effectiveness, improvement of product related to customer/regulatory requirements, resource needs.

requirements.title: Provision of Resources
requirements.intent: Resources are provided for implementing and maintaining the QMS, maintaining its effectiveness, and meeting customer and regulatory requirements.
expected_evidence: evidence of investment in quality controls
failure_modes: resource gaps not escalated to management

requirements.title: Human Resources
requirements.intent: Personnel performing work affecting product quality are competent based on appropriate education, training, skills, and experience. Training needs are evaluated, training is provided, effectiveness is evaluated, and records are maintained.
expected_evidence: records of education, training, skills, and experience
awareness of regulatory requirements and their implications
failure_modes: Competency not defined for roles affecting quality
records not meeting regulatory retention requirements

requirements.title: Infrastructure
requirements.intent: Organization determines, provides, and maintains infrastructure needed for product conformity including buildings, workspace, process equipment, and supporting services.
expected_evidence: contamination control measures appropriate to device classification
failure_modes: contamination controls absent for devices requiring clean environments
infrastructure not meeting device-specific regulatory requirements

requirements.title: Work Environment and Contamination Control
requirements.intent: Work environment is managed to ensure product conformity including conditions for contamination control of microbiologically and/or particulate-contaminated product. Controls must meet applicable regulatory requirements (cleanroom standards, ISO 14644, etc.) for sterile or implantable devices.
expected_evidence: Environmental controls defined per device type
cleanroom classification and monitoring records (where applicable)
failure_modes: no cleaning/disinfection validation for sterile products
requirements.applicability: Required for all — more stringent for sterile and implantable devices.

requirements.title: Planning of Product Realization
requirements.intent: Organization plans and develops processes needed for product realization. Planning is consistent with QMS requirements. Planning determines: quality objectives, processes, documentation, resources, verification/validation/monitoring/inspection activities, records, and risk management activities.
expected_evidence: verification and validation planning for each product
regulatory requirement identification for each product
failure_modes: risk management not planned per ISO 14971
regulatory requirements not identified at product level

requirements.title: Customer-Related Processes
requirements.intent: Requirements related to product are determined (including regulatory requirements, intended use, post-delivery activities). Requirements are reviewed before commitment to supply. Communication with customers includes product information, complaint handling, and advisory notices.
expected_evidence: regulatory requirement identification per product and jurisdiction
failure_modes: regulatory requirements not identified per jurisdiction

requirements.title: Design and Development
requirements.intent: Design and development is planned and controlled. Inputs, outputs, review, verification, validation, and transfer are all controlled and documented. Design changes are controlled. Risk management is integrated throughout.
requirements.applicability: Organizations with design responsibility. 7.3 is the only clause that may be excluded.
requirements.exclusion_condition: Organization does not have design responsibility. Exclusion must be justified and cannot be claimed if regulatory requirements prohibit exclusion.

requirements.title: Design and Development Inputs
requirements.intent: Inputs include: functional and performance requirements, applicable regulatory requirements, outputs of risk management (ISO 14971), and information from previous similar designs.
expected_evidence: risk management outputs feeding into design inputs
completeness and unambiguous review of inputs
failure_modes: risk management not feeding design inputs

requirements.title: Design and Development Outputs
requirements.intent: Outputs meet input requirements, provide production and service information, contain acceptance criteria, and specify essential performance characteristics. Risk controls from ISO 14971 are reflected in design outputs.

requirements.title: Design and Development Review
requirements.intent: Reviews are conducted at suitable stages. Participants include representatives of functions concerned with stage being reviewed. Results and actions recorded.
expected_evidence: Design review records at defined stages
failure_modes: risk management not reviewed at design reviews

requirements.title: Design and Development Verification
requirements.intent: Verification confirms outputs meet input requirements. Methods, results, and conclusions are recorded.
expected_evidence: traceability from verification to specific inputs

requirements.title: Design and Development Validation
requirements.intent: Validation confirms the product meets the requirements for its intended use or application. Performed under defined operating conditions. Clinical evaluation or performance evaluation conducted per applicable regulatory requirements.

requirements.title: Design and Development Transfer
requirements.intent: Organization ensures design and development outputs are transferred to production. Verified that production process is capable of consistently meeting design requirements before formal transfer.
expected_evidence: production documentation verified to design outputs
failure_modes: production documents not verified against design
process capability not confirmed before transfer

requirements.title: Control of Design and Development Changes
requirements.intent: Changes are identified, reviewed, verified, validated as appropriate, and approved before implementation. Effects on component parts, delivered products, and regulatory submissions evaluated.
expected_evidence: regulatory impact evaluation (re-submission or notification required?)

requirements.title: Purchasing
requirements.intent: Purchased product and services conform to requirements. Suppliers are evaluated and selected based on ability to meet requirements including regulatory requirements. Purchasing information specifies requirements. Incoming product is verified.

requirements.title: Purchasing Process
requirements.intent: Supplier evaluation and approval criteria defined. Approved supplier list maintained. Re-evaluation performed. Quality agreements with critical suppliers. Regulatory requirements flowed to suppliers.
expected_evidence: approved supplier list with evaluation records

requirements.title: Purchasing Information
requirements.intent: Purchase orders specify product/service requirements, requirements for approval of products, procedures, processes, equipment, personnel qualification, and QMS requirements as appropriate.
expected_evidence: Purchase order templates with required elements
regulatory requirements on POs for critical items

requirements.title: Verification of Purchased Product
requirements.intent: Organization establishes and implements inspection or other activities for verifying purchased product meets requirements. Records retained.
expected_evidence: first article inspection for new suppliers

requirements.title: Control of Production and Service Provision
requirements.intent: Production under controlled conditions: product information, work instructions, suitable equipment, monitoring and measuring equipment, monitoring and measurement activities, release activities, labeling and packaging activities.

requirements.title: Cleanliness of Product and Contamination Control
requirements.intent: Requirements for product cleanliness established. Contamination controls appropriate to device type and classification. For sterile products: validation of cleaning, disinfection, and sterilization processes.

requirements.title: Installation Activities
requirements.intent: Where installation is required: installation instructions, acceptance criteria, and records of installation maintained.

requirements.title: Servicing Activities
requirements.intent: Where servicing is required: servicing procedures, reference documents, and service records maintained. Service data analyzed as post-market feedback.
expected_evidence: feedback to complaint handling and post-market surveillance
failure_modes: service complaints not entering complaint system

requirements.title: Particular Requirements for Sterile Medical Devices
requirements.intent: Sterile devices: records of sterilization process parameters for each sterilization lot maintained. Sterilization records traceable to each device lot.
expected_evidence: traceability from sterilization record to device lot

requirements.title: Validation of Processes for Production and Service Provision
requirements.intent: Processes whose output cannot be verified by subsequent monitoring and measurement are validated. Validation demonstrates ability to achieve planned results. Includes software used in production and service. Records of validation maintained.

requirements.title: Particular Requirements for Validation of Processes for Sterilization and Sterile Barrier Systems
requirements.intent: Sterilization processes and sterile barrier systems are validated before use. Revalidation performed when changes occur. Records maintained.

requirements.title: Identification
requirements.intent: Product is identified throughout product realization. Identification maintains conformance status. Product identification requirements of applicable regulatory requirements implemented (UDI where required).
expected_evidence: identification at all stages of production

requirements.title: Traceability
requirements.intent: Organization documents traceability procedure. Traceability extends to: components, materials, facilities, and personnel. For implantable devices: traceability to all components, materials, and environmental conditions where those could cause device to not meet its specifications.

requirements.title: General traceability
requirements.intent: Traceability records maintained and available for defined retention period.

requirements.title: Particular requirements for implantable devices
requirements.intent: Records include: all components and materials used; facilities and environmental conditions if required; persons performing inspection; traceability to distributed product.
expected_evidence: device history records with full traceability

requirements.title: Customer Property
requirements.intent: Customer property is identified, verified, protected, and safeguarded. Loss, damage, or unsuitability reported to customer. Includes intellectual property and health data.
failure_modes: patient health data not identified as customer property

requirements.title: Preservation of Product
requirements.intent: Product is preserved during internal processing and delivery. Preservation includes identification, handling, packaging, storage, and protection. For shelf-life controlled items: conditions defined and monitored; expired items controlled.

requirements.title: Control of Monitoring and Measuring Equipment
requirements.intent: Monitoring and measuring equipment is identified, calibrated or verified against traceable standards, adjusted or readjusted as necessary, protected, and safeguarded from tampering. Out-of-tolerance response including assessment of validity of prior measurement results. Software used for monitoring and measuring validated before use.
expected_evidence: OOT response procedure including prior measurement assessment
failure_modes: OOT response without prior measurement assessment
equipment used beyond calibration due date
requirements.applicability: All organizations using measurement equipment for product verification.

requirements.title: General
requirements.intent: Organization plans and implements monitoring, measurement, analysis, and improvement processes. Statistical techniques and their extent of use are determined.

requirements.title: Feedback
requirements.intent: Organization establishes documented procedure for feedback process as an early warning system for quality problems. Sources include post-production, complaints, warranty, servicing data, and communications with customers. Feedback data analyzed and used to monitor compliance with regulatory requirements and to update risk management.
expected_evidence: feedback data collection from all defined sources
feedback trend data at management review
failure_modes: feedback data not at management review
regulatory compliance not monitored via feedback
requirements.applicability: All organizations — one of the most commonly failed ISO 13485 clauses.

requirements.title: Internal Audit
requirements.intent: Internal audits conducted at planned intervals to determine if QMS conforms to ISO 13485 AND applicable regulatory requirements, and is effectively implemented and maintained. Audit program planned based on risk. Auditors objective and impartial. Results reported to management. Corrective actions without undue delay.

requirements.title: Monitoring and Measurement of Processes
requirements.intent: Organization applies suitable methods to monitor and measure QMS processes. Methods demonstrate ability to achieve planned results. When planned results not achieved, corrective action taken as appropriate.

requirements.title: Monitoring and Measurement of Product
requirements.intent: Product characteristics are monitored and measured at appropriate stages. Records indicate: conformance to criteria, personnel performing release, release date. Product not released until planned arrangements have been satisfactorily completed or approved by relevant authority and applicable regulatory requirements met.
expected_evidence: no release without completion of planned inspection
failure_modes: personnel not identified on release records
product released before all planned activities completed

requirements.title: Control of Nonconforming Product
requirements.intent: Product that does not conform to product requirements is identified and controlled to prevent unintended use or delivery. Nonconforming product is dealt with: rework, concession (with regulatory notification for regulatory submissions), return, or scrap. Reworked product re-inspected. Concessions require regulatory authority approval where required. Records of concessions and escapes maintained.
expected_evidence: concession records with regulatory approval where required
failure_modes: concessions without regulatory approval where required
no customer notification for escaped product

requirements.title: Analysis of Data
requirements.intent: Organization determines, collects, and analyzes appropriate data to demonstrate suitability and effectiveness of QMS and to evaluate where improvement can be made. Data includes: customer feedback, conformity to product requirements, process and product characteristics and trends, suppliers, audit results, service reports.
expected_evidence: analysis records covering all required sources
results feeding CAPA and management review

requirements.title: Continual Improvement
requirements.intent: Organization continually improves QMS effectiveness through quality policy, objectives, audit results, analysis of data, corrective and preventive actions, and management review. Implements any changes to applicable regulatory requirements applicable to the medical device.
expected_evidence: connection of improvement to data analysis and audit results
failure_modes: management review recommendations not followed through

requirements.title: Corrective Action
requirements.intent: Corrective action taken to eliminate causes of nonconformities to prevent recurrence, proportionate to effects. Includes: reviewing nonconformities including complaints, determining causes, evaluating need for action to prevent recurrence, implementing action, recording results, reviewing action taken, and notifying regulatory authorities where required.

requirements.title: Preventive Action
requirements.intent: Organization determines action to eliminate causes of potential nonconformities to prevent their occurrence. Includes: identifying potential nonconformities and causes, evaluating need for action, implementing action, recording results, reviewing action taken.
expected_evidence: preventive action records based on risk analysis and trend data
failure_modes: risk analysis not connected to preventive action
trend data not driving preventive actions

requirements.title: Complaint Handling and Regulatory Reporting
requirements.intent: Complaint handling system meets ISO 13485:2016 requirements AND applicable regulatory requirements for vigilance reporting, adverse event reporting, and MDR. A documented procedure defines: what constitutes a complaint; investigation process; timeframes; reportability decision; authority notification; records.
expected_evidence: Complaint handling procedure with ISO 13485 definition applied
failure_modes: Narrow complaint definition excluding oral or electronic
complaints not generating CARs for systemic issues
service reports not entering complaint system
records not meeting regulatory retention requirements
requirements.applicability: All organizations — Critical applicability; absent complaint system is always a major finding.

requirements.title: QMSR Applicability Determination
requirements.intent: The QMSR applies to manufacturers of finished devices intended for commercial distribution in the US. Includes: manufacturers of components and parts if the manufacturer is also the finished device manufacturer; contract manufacturers performing production or labeling operations; foreign manufacturers exporting to the US.
expected_evidence: authorized US agent designated for foreign manufacturers
failure_modes: Organization manufactures for US market but not registered
no US agent for foreign manufacturer

requirements.title: Design History File
requirements.intent: The organization maintains a Design History File (DHF) for each type of device. The DHF contains or references records demonstrating the device was designed in accordance with the approved design plan and requirements. All design control records are organized and locatable per device type.
expected_evidence: DHF index or structure per device type
all required design records present or referenced: design plan, inputs, outputs, reviews, verification, validation, transfer
DHF demonstrating device was designed per the approved plan
failure_modes: No DHF defined per device type
DHF is a folder of miscellaneous records without demonstrating design was conducted per plan
records in DHF not approved or dated
requirements.applicability: Organizations with design responsibility — Class II and III devices especially.
requirements.note: "Design History File" is the QSR/QMSR term; ISO 13485 equivalent is design and development records per Clause 7.3.

requirements.title: Design Change Submission Evaluation
requirements.intent: Changes to cleared or approved devices are evaluated for 510(k)/PMA supplement requirement before implementation. Organization has a process to make this determination and documents the basis for decisions not to submit.
expected_evidence: Design change procedure with submission evaluation step
records of 510(k)/PMA impact assessment for all design changes
changes requiring submission not implemented until clearance/approval
failure_modes: Design changes implemented without regulatory impact assessment
changes made to cleared device without evaluating submission need
requirements.applicability: Organizations with cleared or approved devices.

requirements.title: Device Master Record
requirements.intent: Organization maintains a Device Master Record (DMR) for each type of device, or the location of the DMR. The DMR includes or references: device specifications (drawings, composition, formulation, component specifications, software specifications), production process specifications (manufacturing procedures, equipment, workmanship standards, acceptance criteria), quality assurance procedures and specifications, packaging and labeling specifications, installation and maintenance procedures.
expected_evidence: specifications, procedures, and quality assurance documents listed and locatable
DMR current and consistent with cleared/approved specifications
revision control demonstrating DMR is to current approved state
failure_modes: DMR is a list of procedures not specific to the device
DMR not reflecting current cleared/approved specification
content not meeting minimum required elements
requirements.regulatory_reference: 21 CFR 820.181 (QSR) / QMSR equivalent within ISO 13485 7.5 production documentation.
requirements.note: "Device Master Record" is the QSR/QMSR term; ISO 13485 equivalent is the production documentation set.

requirements.title: Device History Record
requirements.intent: Organization maintains a Device History Record (DHR) for each manufactured device or batch. The DHR demonstrates the device was manufactured in accordance with the DMR. DHR contents include: dates of manufacture, quantity manufactured, quantity released for distribution, acceptance records demonstrating conformity, primary identification label and labeling, and UDI (where applicable).
failure_modes: DHR not demonstrating conformance to DMR
no traceability from DHR to components
DHR not retained for required period (2 years minimum from manufacture date)
requirements.regulatory_reference: 21 CFR 820.184 (QSR) / QMSR equivalent within ISO 13485 7.5 records of production.
requirements.note: "Device History Record" is the QSR/QMSR term; ISO 13485 uses "records of production."

requirements.title: MDR Reporting Procedure
requirements.intent: Organization has a documented procedure for evaluating events and complaints for MDR reportability under 21 CFR Part 803. Procedure defines: reportable event criteria, responsible personnel, submission form (MedWatch 3500A / eMDR), timeframes, follow-up report process, and records retention.

requirements.title: MDR Reportability Criteria
requirements.intent: Organization's complaint evaluation process includes explicit MDR reportability evaluation. Evaluates whether a complaint or event involves: device malfunction that could cause or contribute to serious injury or death if it were to recur; patient death or serious injury reasonably suggested to be caused by the device.
expected_evidence: Reportability decision tree or criteria checklist
complaint evaluation records showing MDR assessment
definition of "serious injury" per 21 CFR 803.3 applied
records of events evaluated and not reported (with rationale)
failure_modes: Complaints evaluated but no MDR assessment
"serious injury" defined more narrowly than 21 CFR 803.3

requirements.title: MDR Reporting Timeframes
requirements.intent: MDR reports are submitted within required timeframes:
expected_evidence: complaint handling records showing date of awareness vs. date of MDR submission
tracking system for open MDR obligations

requirements.title: MDR Records Retention
requirements.intent: Organization retains MDR-related records for 2 years from the date of the event or from the date of submission — whichever is later. Records include: complaint files, MDR event files, MDR submissions, and any internal review records.
expected_evidence: MDR record retention schedule meeting 2-year minimum

requirements.title: Corrections and Removals Procedure
requirements.intent: Organization has a documented procedure for managing, documenting, and reporting corrections and removals under 21 CFR Part 806. A "correction" is repair, modification, adjustment, relabeling, destruction, or inspection without removing from distribution. A "removal" is removing a product from distribution.
expected_evidence: reporting threshold criteria (whether action reduces risk of serious adverse health consequences)
records of all corrections and removals
failure_modes: records of all corrections/removals not maintained

requirements.title: Corrections and Removals Records
requirements.intent: Records are maintained for all corrections and removals regardless of whether FDA reporting was required. Records include: device name, model number, dates, number of devices, reason for action, failure investigation, corrective action, distribution data.
expected_evidence: Records for all corrections and removals

requirements.title: UDI Implementation
requirements.intent: Organization has implemented Unique Device Identification per 21 CFR Parts 801 and 830. Device labels bear UDI in required format (HIBC or GS1). UDI information submitted to GUDID (Global Unique Device Identification Database). UDI appears in DHR for each production unit/lot.
expected_evidence: UDI labeling on all required devices
UDI issuing agency certification (GS1 or HIBCC)
failure_modes: UDI implementation timeline not met for device class
requirements.applicability: All device manufacturers — class-specific implementation timelines applied.

requirements.title: FDA Complaint Handling Requirements
requirements.intent: Complaint files contain FDA-required information beyond ISO 13485 base requirements: identity of device, date complaint received, name/address/phone of complainant, complaint details, results of investigation, response to complainant. Complaints evaluated for MDR reportability.
expected_evidence: Complaint records with all required elements
MDR evaluation documented in complaint record
failure_modes: MDR evaluation not documented in complaint file

requirements.title: Establishment Registration and Device Listing
requirements.intent: Organization maintains current FDA establishment registration and device listing. Registration renewed annually. Device listing accurately reflects all devices manufactured. Foreign manufacturers designate authorized US agent.
expected_evidence: US agent designation for foreign manufacturers
device listing accuracy vs. devices manufactured
failure_modes: no US agent for foreign manufacturer

requirements.title: FDA Inspection Preparation
requirements.intent: Organization is able to present records in response to FDA investigator requests during inspections. Records must be organized, accessible, and in English (or accompanied by certified translation). Response to 483 observations is documented and tracked.
expected_evidence: Record management system enabling rapid retrieval
English language records or certified translations
483 observation response tracking (for organizations with prior inspections)
failure_modes: Records not retrievable within reasonable time

requirements.title: Regulatory Requirements Identification (Multi-Authority)
requirements.intent: Organization identifies applicable regulatory requirements for every in-scope jurisdiction and maintains a process to monitor and implement changes. Each jurisdiction's requirements are mapped to QMS processes.
expected_evidence: process for monitoring regulatory changes in each jurisdiction
management review input for each jurisdiction's regulatory status
failure_modes: regulatory change monitoring limited to one country
jurisdiction requirements not mapped to QMS
management review does not address multi-authority regulatory status

requirements.title: US Marketing Authorization and Registration
requirements.intent: Organization maintains current FDA establishment registration, device listing, and 510(k)/PMA clearance/approval for all US market devices. All are accurate and current.
expected_evidence: device listing per all marketed devices
510(k) clearance or PMA approval per device

requirements.title: Health Canada Marketing Authorization
requirements.intent: Organization maintains current Medical Device Licence (MDL) for Class II–IV devices and Establishment Licence for manufacturing activities in Canada. Devices classified per Canadian Medical Device Regulations (CMDR).
expected_evidence: Current MDL per device or device family
changes to devices evaluated for licence amendment
failure_modes: licence amendments not pursued when required

requirements.title: ANVISA Registration (Brazil)
requirements.intent: Organization maintains current ANVISA Registro (product registration) for devices sold in Brazil. Foreign manufacturers designate a Brazilian Titular Registration Holder. Brazilian GMP (CBPF) compliance demonstrated.
failure_modes: registration scope not covering all sold devices

requirements.title: TGA ARTG Inclusion (Australia)
requirements.intent: Organization maintains current ARTG (Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods) inclusion for devices sold in Australia. TGA GMP clearance held for manufacturing. Conformity assessment certification current.

requirements.title: PMDA / MHLW Authorization (Japan)
requirements.intent: Organization maintains current MHLW/PMDA approval for devices sold in Japan. Local Marketing Authorization Holder (MAH) designated. Quality Assurance Person (QAP) designated per Japanese QMS Ordinance.
expected_evidence: PMDA approval scope covering all sold devices
failure_modes: QAP not designated or not qualified

requirements.title: Health Canada Vigilance Reporting
requirements.intent: Organization has a procedure for evaluating and reporting Mandatory Problem Reports (MPR) and Medical Incident Reports (MIR) to Health Canada. Timeframes: death or serious injury — 10 days; potential for serious injury — 30 days.
expected_evidence: Vigilance reporting procedure with HC-specific criteria and timeframes
reportability evaluation process per Health Canada requirements
records of events evaluated but not reported (with rationale)
failure_modes: no records of HC reportability evaluation

extra_fields.MDSAP Grade: Grade 3 for absent HC reporting process.

requirements.title: ANVISA Vigilance Reporting (Brazil)
requirements.intent: Organization evaluates and reports adverse events to ANVISA per Brazilian requirements. Serious adverse events: 15 days. Non-serious: 30 days. Local Titular holder coordinates Brazilian reporting.
expected_evidence: Titular holder role in reporting defined

extra_fields.MDSAP Grade: Grade 3 for absent ANVISA reporting process.

requirements.title: TGA Mandatory Problem Reporting (Australia)
requirements.intent: Organization evaluates and reports adverse events to TGA (or Australian Sponsor) per TGA requirements. Timeframes: death — 2 days; serious injury — 10 days; non-serious — 30 days.
expected_evidence: TGA vigilance procedure with specific timeframes
failure_modes: TGA timeframes not defined (especially 2-day for death)

extra_fields.MDSAP Grade: Grade 3 for absent TGA reporting process; Grade 4 if 2-day death reporting not addressed.

requirements.title: PMDA Vigilance Reporting (Japan)
requirements.intent: Organization evaluates adverse events for PMDA reporting per GVP Ordinance through the Japanese MAH. Serious incidents reported within 15 days (death or serious injury); others within 30 days.
expected_evidence: MAH role in Japanese reporting defined

extra_fields.MDSAP Grade: Grade 3 for absent PMDA reporting process.

requirements.title: Health Canada Corrections and Recalls
requirements.intent: Organization has a procedure for managing and reporting recalls to Health Canada per CMDR requirements. Recalls reported to Health Canada; effectiveness checks conducted; Health Canada notifications tracked.
expected_evidence: Health Canada notification records for recalls
failure_modes: Health Canada not notified for reportable recalls

extra_fields.MDSAP Grade: Grade 3 for absent HC recall reporting process.

requirements.title: Design Documentation Multi-Authority Requirements
requirements.intent: Design documentation satisfies all in-scope jurisdiction requirements simultaneously. ISO 13485 7.3 is the base; FDA requires DHF structure; EU MDR requires technical documentation per Annex II.
expected_evidence: Design documentation addressing all in-scope jurisdiction requirements
design change evaluation for all jurisdictions simultaneously
regulatory submission impact assessment covers all in-scope jurisdictions
failure_modes: Design documentation only structured for one jurisdiction
design change evaluation only evaluates one authority's notification requirements
technical documentation gaps for EU MDR if EU is in scope
requirements.applicability: Organizations with design responsibility selling to multiple jurisdictions.

requirements.title: Multi-Jurisdiction Record Retention
requirements.intent: Record retention periods meet the most stringent requirement across all in-scope jurisdictions. Different authorities have different minimums. Organization uses the longest applicable period for each record type.
expected_evidence: Record retention schedule with per-jurisdiction retention periods identified
failure_modes: Retention schedule based on one jurisdiction only
records destroyed at minimum period when another jurisdiction requires longer
no comparison of retention requirements across jurisdictions

requirements.title: Supplier Flow-Down Multi-Authority Requirements
requirements.intent: Supplier controls flow down requirements from all in-scope regulatory authorities. Purchase orders and quality agreements reference applicable jurisdiction requirements where supplier activities affect regulatory compliance.
expected_evidence: Quality agreements referencing all applicable regulatory requirements per jurisdiction
PO requirements including jurisdiction-specific requirements where applicable
supplier audit scope including multi-authority requirements
failure_modes: Quality agreements reference only one jurisdiction's requirements
supplier controls not considering multi-authority requirements
regulatory flow-down limited to one country
requirements.applicability: All MDSAP-enrolled organizations with critical suppliers.

requirements.title: Technical Documentation (Annex II)
requirements.intent: Technical documentation per EU MDR Annex II is maintained for each device. Includes: device description and specification, information supplied by manufacturer, design and manufacturing information, general safety and performance requirements, benefit-risk analysis, product verification and validation.
expected_evidence: Technical documentation index per Annex II
failure_modes: Technical documentation not structured per Annex II
Notified Body review records not retained
requirements.applicability: Manufacturers of Class IIa, IIb, III devices / implantable devices in EU.

requirements.title: Clinical Evaluation (Article 61)
requirements.intent: Clinical evaluation is conducted and documented per Article 61 and MDCG 2020-13. Evaluation is current, systematic, and based on clinical data. PMCF plan established. Clinical evaluation report (CER) updated per periodic review schedule.
expected_evidence: clinical data sources (clinical investigation, literature, PMCF)
failure_modes: clinical evaluation based on literature only without systematic methodology
equivalence without contractual access to technical documentation
requirements.applicability: All EU MDR device classes — most critical for Class III / implantable.

requirements.title: Periodic Safety Update Report (Article 86)
requirements.intent: PSUR is produced at required frequency: Class III / implantable — annually; Class IIa / IIb — every 2 years. PSUR includes analysis of post-market data, conclusions on benefit-risk, and update to clinical evaluation.
expected_evidence: linkage to PMS data and clinical evaluation update
failure_modes: not linked to PMS data or CER update
requirements.applicability: Class IIa, IIb, III device manufacturers with EU market access.

requirements.title: Summary of Safety and Clinical Performance (Article 32)
requirements.intent: SSCP published in EUDAMED for all Class III devices and implantable devices. SSCP reviewed and updated at least annually; every update validated by Notified Body.
expected_evidence: SSCP content per Annex I Article 32 requirements
failure_modes: not validated by Notified Body after update
requirements.applicability: Class III and implantable device manufacturers with EU market access.

requirements.title: EU Authorised Representative and PRRC
requirements.intent: Non-EU manufacturers designate an EU Authorised Representative (EUAR). The manufacturer (or its EU representative) designates a Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) with defined qualifications.
expected_evidence: PRRC qualification documentation (per Annex VII Article 15)
failure_modes: PRRC role not defined in QMS
requirements.applicability: Non-EU device manufacturers selling to EU; EU manufacturers must designate PRRC.

requirements.title: UDI per EU MDR
requirements.intent: Devices placed on EU market bear UDI per EU MDR Article 27. UDI-DI and UDI-PI assigned. UDI uploaded to EUDAMED. UDI-DI linked to technical documentation.
expected_evidence: UDI labeling per EU MDR requirements
requirements.applicability: All device classes per EU MDR UDI implementation timelines.

requirements.title: Serious Incident Reporting (EU MDR Article 87)
requirements.intent: Serious incidents involving EU market devices are reported to the appropriate competent authority (or through EUDAMED when fully operational) within required timeframes: immediately (no later than 2 days) for serious public health threat; 10 days for death or unanticipated serious deterioration; 15 days for other serious incidents.
expected_evidence: EU MDR serious incident reporting procedure with specific timeframes
competent authority contact list per EU member state
failure_modes: No EU MDR-specific reporting criteria or timeframes
requirements.applicability: All manufacturers with EU market access for MDR-regulated devices.

requirements.title: Understanding the Organization and Its Context
requirements.intent: Organization identifies internal and external issues relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended outcomes of the EMS, including the environmental conditions it affects or is affected by.
expected_evidence: Context analysis including environmental conditions (climate, ecology, pollution levels)
external issues (regulatory landscape, community expectations, environmental conditions)
linkage to EMS scope and planning
failure_modes: Context analysis has no environmental content — mirrors ISO 9001 analysis without EMS-specific content
analysis performed once and never updated

requirements.title: Understanding the Needs and Expectations of Interested Parties
requirements.intent: Organization identifies interested parties relevant to the EMS and their environmental requirements and expectations, including regulatory authorities, community, employees, customers, and suppliers.
expected_evidence: Interested party register with environmental requirements per party
regulatory authorities listed with applicable requirements
requirements linked to compliance obligations evaluation
failure_modes: interested party requirements not linked to compliance obligations

requirements.title: Determining the Scope of the EMS
requirements.intent: Scope is defined considering context, interested party requirements, organizational units, activities, products and services, and the organization's authority and ability to exercise control and influence. Scope is documented and available.
expected_evidence: documented and available to interested parties
failure_modes: significant environmental activities excluded without justification

requirements.title: Environmental Management System
requirements.intent: Organization establishes, implements, maintains, and continually improves the EMS including the processes needed and their interactions.
expected_evidence: Process map or EMS process description
failure_modes: EMS exists as a separate paper system with no integration into operations
EMS processes not defined or mapped

requirements.title: Leadership and Commitment
requirements.intent: Top management demonstrates leadership and commitment to the EMS through accountability, ensuring the EMS achieves its intended outcomes, communicating environmental management importance, and supporting continual improvement.
expected_evidence: Top management participation in management review
environmental performance included in business reporting
failure_modes: EMS managed entirely by environmental coordinator with no top management involvement
management review attended by quality/environment staff only
no evidence of top management accountability for environmental performance

requirements.title: Environmental Policy
requirements.intent: Environmental policy is appropriate to the organization's context (including the nature, scale, and environmental impacts of its activities), commits to compliance with legal requirements, commits to continual improvement of environmental performance, and provides framework for environmental objectives.
expected_evidence: Policy signed and dated by top management
content appropriate to organization's scale and impacts
failure_modes: Policy is generic text not reflecting actual activities or impacts

requirements.title: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
requirements.intent: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities for EMS are assigned and communicated. Top management assigns responsibility for EMS conformance and environmental performance reporting.
expected_evidence: specific assignment of responsibility for reporting environmental performance to top management
backup/deputy roles for key EMS functions
failure_modes: All EMS responsibilities assigned to one person with no backup
no defined responsibility for performance reporting to top management

requirements.title: Actions to Address Risks and Opportunities (EMS)
requirements.intent: Organization considers environmental conditions, aspects and impacts, legal requirements, and interested party needs to determine risks and opportunities that need to be addressed. Plans actions proportionate to risk.
expected_evidence: risks linked to aspects and legal requirements
failure_modes: Risk assessment is generic business risk without EMS content
no linkage between risks and EMS planning

requirements.title: Environmental Aspects and Impacts
requirements.intent: Organization identifies environmental aspects of its activities, products, and services within defined scope and life cycle perspective, determines actual and potential impacts, and determines significant environmental aspects (SEAs) using established criteria.
expected_evidence: life cycle perspective applied (upstream inputs, production, use by others, end of life)
aspects register covering all activities, products, services, and abnormal/emergency conditions
failure_modes: Only normal operations considered — abnormal and emergency conditions absent
significance criteria not documented or not applied consistently
requirements.applicability: All organizations — the foundational EMS planning element.

requirements.title: Compliance Obligations
requirements.intent: Organization determines legal requirements (federal, state/provincial, local, permit conditions) and voluntary commitments (industry codes, community agreements, voluntary programs) applicable to its environmental aspects. These are accessible, updated, and considered in planning.
expected_evidence: specific regulations listed with relevant sections
linkage to aspects and operational controls
failure_modes: Register lists regulation titles only — no specific applicable sections
no process for identifying new requirements
register not reviewed after regulatory changes
no linkage to aspects or controls
requirements.applicability: All organizations — one of the most commonly failed ISO 14001 requirements.

requirements.title: Planning Actions
requirements.intent: Organization plans actions to address SEAs, compliance obligations, risks, and opportunities. Actions are integrated into EMS processes and may include operational controls, environmental objectives, and emergency preparedness.
expected_evidence: Action planning records linking SEAs to controls
compliance obligations linked to operational controls and monitoring
integration of actions into operational procedures
failure_modes: Planning exists in theory but not integrated into operational procedures
actions planned but not assigned or implemented

requirements.title: Environmental Objectives and Planning
requirements.intent: Environmental objectives are established at relevant functions, are consistent with policy, are measurable (where practicable), consider SEAs and compliance obligations, are monitored, are communicated, and are updated. Plans specify who, what, resources, timeline, and how evaluated.
expected_evidence: Environmental objectives documented with measurable targets
linkage to SEAs and policy commitments
programs with responsible owners and timelines
failure_modes: objectives unchanged year over year regardless of performance
objectives not communicated beyond environmental department

requirements.title: Resources
requirements.intent: Resources (personnel, infrastructure, technology, financial) are provided for EMS establishment, implementation, maintenance, and improvement.
expected_evidence: evidence of investment in environmental controls
failure_modes: EMS functions with no dedicated resources
resource gaps not escalated to management

requirements.title: Competence
requirements.intent: Persons performing work affecting EMS performance are competent. Competence includes education, training, or experience appropriate to SEA management, compliance management, and emergency response.
expected_evidence: competency assessment for key EMS functions
failure_modes: competency assessed by attendance not by evaluation

requirements.title: Awareness
requirements.intent: All persons doing work under the organization's control are aware of the environmental policy, significant aspects related to their work, their contribution to EMS effectiveness, and the consequences of not conforming to EMS requirements (including potential legal consequences).
expected_evidence: ability of personnel (including contractors) to demonstrate SEA awareness
failure_modes: operators unaware of significant aspects in their area

requirements.title: Communication
requirements.intent: Internal and external communication related to the EMS is planned and executed. What, when, with whom, and how communicated. Environmental performance communicated externally as appropriate.
expected_evidence: records of internal communications (policy updates, SEA changes, incident reports)
external communication records (regulatory, community, public environmental reports)
failure_modes: no process for communicating environmental incidents

requirements.title: Documented Information
requirements.intent: Documented information required by ISO 14001:2015 and determined necessary by the organization is created, maintained, and controlled. Includes: EMS scope, policy, aspects and impacts, legal register, objectives, operational controls, monitoring records, and competence records.
expected_evidence: All required EMS documents identified and controlled
retention periods defined for environmental records
failure_modes: retention periods not addressing regulatory requirements (some permits require multi-year record retention)
environmental permits not treated as controlled documents

requirements.title: Operational Planning and Control
requirements.intent: Organization establishes, implements, controls, and maintains processes needed to meet EMS requirements for SEAs, compliance obligations, and planned actions. Controls include eliminating deviations, maintaining operational criteria, and controlling outsourced processes and product/service procurement.
expected_evidence: Operational control procedures linked to specific SEAs
operational criteria (limits, parameters, conditions) defined in procedures
contractor and supplier controls for environmental impact
failure_modes: Generic environmental procedures not linked to specific SEAs
procurement does not consider environmental impacts
life cycle perspective absent from supply chain controls
requirements.applicability: All organizations — procedures must link to SEAs, not be generic.

requirements.title: Emergency Preparedness and Response
requirements.intent: Organization prepares for and responds to potential environmental emergencies and accidents. Response procedures exist for identified scenarios. Procedures tested at defined frequency. Regulatory notification included. Lessons learned from tests and actual events incorporated.
expected_evidence: emergency response procedure for each credible scenario
review and update after tests and incidents
failure_modes: only fire/safety emergencies addressed — environmental spill and release scenarios absent
tests conducted but no lessons learned
requirements.applicability: All organizations with environmental risk — one of the most consistently failed ISO 14001 clauses.

requirements.title: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis, and Evaluation
requirements.intent: Organization monitors and measures environmental performance parameters linked to significant aspects and compliance obligations. Methods, criteria, frequency, and timing defined. Results analyzed and evaluated against objectives and compliance thresholds. Records maintained.
expected_evidence: parameters linked to SEAs and legal requirements
results analyzed against targets and legal limits
failure_modes: records not retained per regulatory requirements

requirements.title: Evaluation of Compliance
requirements.intent: Organization evaluates compliance with its legal and other requirements at planned intervals. Records of compliance evaluation results are maintained. Actions taken for findings of noncompliance.
expected_evidence: evaluation records covering all legal requirements and permit conditions
failure_modes: compliance assumed based on no violations
noncompliance findings not generating corrective actions
requirements.applicability: All organizations — one of the most consistently audited and failed ISO 14001 requirements.

requirements.title: Internal Audit
requirements.intent: Internal audit program covers all EMS elements including environmental compliance requirements. Auditors are competent and objective. Findings reach management. Corrective actions are generated for findings.
expected_evidence: environmental compliance as audit scope element
failure_modes: Audit covers EMS documents only — no compliance assessment
auditors not qualified in environmental regulations
compliance evaluation not part of audit scope

requirements.title: Management Review
requirements.intent: Top management reviews EMS at planned intervals for continuing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness. All required inputs reviewed. Outputs include decisions and actions.
expected_evidence: action items with owners and timelines
failure_modes: Environmental performance data not presented in trend form

extra_fields.Required Outputs: Conclusions on continuing suitability/adequacy/effectiveness; continual improvement opportunities; any changes to EMS including objectives; resource needs; actions if objectives not achieved.

requirements.title: General Improvement
requirements.intent: Organization determines opportunities for improvement and implements actions to achieve intended EMS outcomes and enhance environmental performance.
expected_evidence: linkage between monitoring results and improvement actions
failure_modes: analysis results not converting to actions

requirements.title: Nonconformity and Corrective Action
requirements.intent: Nonconformities (including compliance failures) are reacted to, root causes determined, corrective actions implemented, and effectiveness verified. Regulatory reporting obligations addressed when compliance failures occur.
expected_evidence: CAR records with root cause analysis
regulatory notification records for compliance failures
failure_modes: Compliance failures corrected but not treated as nonconformities

requirements.title: Continual Improvement
requirements.intent: Organization continually improves EMS suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness to enhance environmental performance. Evidence of improvement over time is required.
expected_evidence: Environmental performance trend data showing improvement
failure_modes: No evidence of improvement over certification cycle
management review recommends improvements but no follow-through

requirements.title: Customer-Specific Requirements
requirements.intent: Organization identifies and implements applicable customer-specific requirements (CSRs) for all customers it supplies. CSRs supplement IATF 16949 and are treated as mandatory requirements within the QMS scope. CSRs are reviewed when customers issue updates.
expected_evidence: CSR register or matrix listing applicable CSRs per customer
evidence CSRs have been obtained (documented download or receipt)
gap analysis against each applicable CSR
implementation of CSR requirements in relevant procedures
failure_modes: CSRs obtained but not implemented in procedures
no review process for CSR updates
only one customer's CSRs considered when multiple customers supply to the site
requirements.applicability: All organizations supplying to OEM customers with published CSRs.

requirements.title: Product and Process Conformity
requirements.intent: Organization plans and controls processes for conformity of products and processes including: prevention of nonconforming product, escalation process for out-of-control or nonconforming situations, and risk analysis for containment of customer-impacting concerns.
failure_modes: conformity planning generic without customer-specific considerations

requirements.title: Corporate Accountability
requirements.intent: Top management demonstrates accountability for customer satisfaction and QMS effectiveness through defined responsibilities, authority structures, and active participation — not solely through delegation to quality function.
expected_evidence: Top management accountabilities defined in QMS
evidence of top management involvement in customer satisfaction reviews
escalation from quality to top management documented
failure_modes: All quality accountability delegated to quality manager
top management absent from customer satisfaction reviews

requirements.title: Risk Analysis
requirements.intent: Risk analysis includes lessons learned from product recalls, product audits, field returns, warranty claims, and customer notifications. Risk analysis outputs are used in APQP and corrective action planning.
expected_evidence: Risk analysis incorporating warranty and field return data
product recall history in risk inputs
risk analysis linkage to APQP inputs
failure_modes: Risk analysis does not incorporate historical failure data
warranty data not feeding risk assessment
FMEA not informed by lessons learned
risk analysis a standalone exercise not connected to planning

requirements.title: Preventive Action
requirements.intent: Organization implements a systematic preventive action process using risk analysis tools (FMEA, mistake-proofing, SPC) to eliminate potential causes of nonconformance before they occur.
expected_evidence: risk analysis tools (FMEA, SPC control limits, poka-yoke) applied proactively
failure_modes: Preventive action addressed as corrective action with earlier timing
no systematic identification of potential nonconformances
risk tools applied reactively rather than proactively

requirements.title: Plant, Facility, and Equipment Planning
requirements.intent: Plant layout is planned to optimize material flow, minimize transport and handling, facilitate value-added processing, and support quality. Equipment is maintained using a Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) approach with OEE tracking.
expected_evidence: preventive maintenance schedules for all key equipment

requirements.title: Measurement System Analysis (MSA)
requirements.intent: Measurement systems used for monitoring and measurement of special characteristics and for product verification are analyzed using MSA studies. Studies are conducted at APQP stage and repeated when measurement systems change. Acceptability criteria applied per AIAG MSA manual.
expected_evidence: MSA procedure referencing AIAG MSA methodology
GR&R study records for variable measurement systems
attribute MSA (kappa study) for attribute gauges
acceptability criteria (≤10% preferred, ≤30% acceptable with justification)
failure_modes: MSA conducted but results not evaluated against criteria
failed MSA studies with no remediation
MSA not repeated after measurement system changes
requirements.applicability: Required for all measurement systems referenced in control plans — no exception.

requirements.title: Internal Laboratory
requirements.intent: Internal measurement and testing laboratory has a defined scope of laboratory services, is competent to perform the required services, and is controlled per a documented system equivalent to ISO/IEC 17025 scope.
expected_evidence: personnel competency records for laboratory activities
failure_modes: equipment not all in calibration program
personnel competency not defined or assessed

requirements.title: Automotive Product-Related Training
requirements.intent: Personnel performing tasks affecting product quality are trained on applicable customer-specific requirements and quality-related topics. Training is competency-based not attendance-based. Training effectiveness is evaluated.
expected_evidence: Training needs analysis incorporating CSR requirements
operator certification for processes with special characteristics
failure_modes: CSR requirements not included in training content
no operator certification for SC processes

requirements.title: Record Retention
requirements.intent: Record retention requirements meet IATF 16949 minimum requirements and customer-specific record retention requirements. Production records, PPAP records, and tooling records are retained for the active production period plus customer-specified duration.
expected_evidence: Record retention schedule with product type and customer-specific retention periods
PPAP records retained for active production life plus customer minimum
tooling records retained while tooling is active
failure_modes: Record retention schedule does not meet customer minimums
PPAP records destroyed after product becomes obsolete
generic retention schedule not accounting for automotive requirements

requirements.title: Operational Planning — Customer Requirements and CSR
requirements.intent: Operational planning incorporates customer requirements and applicable CSRs. Plans address product and process special characteristics, statutory and regulatory requirements, and customer-specific requirements for manufacturing.
expected_evidence: Quality plans or control plans incorporating customer-specific controls
CSR requirements reflected in operational planning
failure_modes: Operational planning does not incorporate CSR requirements
special characteristics not addressed in operational plans

requirements.title: APQP and Multidisciplinary Approach
requirements.intent: Product realization is planned using Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) methodology with a multidisciplinary team. APQP includes DFMEA/PFMEA development, control plan creation, PPAP planning, and customer milestone management.
expected_evidence: DFMEA and PFMEA timing relative to product launch
failure_modes: APQP conducted individually not as multidisciplinary team
FMEA not completed before production start
control plan not developed before launch
requirements.applicability: All organizations developing new or revised products or processes.

requirements.title: Special Characteristics
requirements.intent: Special characteristics (SCs) are identified from all sources (customer-designated, DFMEA, PFMEA, field experience). SCs are classified per applicable customer symbol convention, cascaded to all relevant planning documents, and communicated to operators.
expected_evidence: SC cascade to control plans and WIs
failure_modes: SCs from PFMEA not cascaded to control plans
SC not identified on production drawings or planning documents
SCs treated identically to non-SCs in control
requirements.applicability: All organizations with designated special characteristics.

requirements.title: Design FMEA (DFMEA)
requirements.intent: DFMEA is conducted for all products with design responsibility using AIAG/VDA FMEA methodology. DFMEA is completed before design verification. Action Priority (AP) replaces RPN. High AP actions are addressed before design release.
expected_evidence: high AP actions addressed before design release
failure_modes: DFMEA not updated after design changes

requirements.title: Process FMEA (PFMEA)
requirements.intent: PFMEA is conducted for all manufacturing processes using AIAG/VDA FMEA methodology. PFMEA is linked to control plan. AP used for prioritization. PFMEA updated when processes change or nonconformances occur. PFMEA lessons learned integrated from historical data.
expected_evidence: linkage between PFMEA failure modes and control plan controls
PFMEA update records after process changes
failure_modes: no linkage between PFMEA and control plan
PFMEA not updated after process changes
PFMEA conducted by quality alone without engineering and operations

requirements.title: Manufacturing Process Design Output
requirements.intent: Manufacturing process design outputs include: control plans (family or individual), work instructions, process flow diagrams, and all documents necessary to control production. These outputs are linked and consistent with PFMEA.
expected_evidence: work instructions consistent with control plan steps
process flow diagrams matching production sequence
consistency across PFMEA, control plan, and WI verified
failure_modes: Control plans not linked to PFMEA
work instructions inconsistent with control plans
process flow does not match actual production
PFMEA failure modes not reflected in control plan controls

requirements.title: Control Plan
requirements.intent: Control plans exist for pre-launch and production phases. Control plans include: part/process identification, process steps, product and process characteristics, special characteristics with symbol, control method, sample size and frequency, reaction plan, and MSA study reference. Control plans are updated when processes change.
expected_evidence: reaction plans defined for each control
MSA study referenced for measurement systems
failure_modes: SCs not identified or identified without customer symbols
control plan not updated after process changes
family control plan used where individual required by customer CSR
requirements.applicability: All organizations — one of the most consistently audited IATF documents.

requirements.title: Work Instructions
requirements.intent: Work instructions exist for all operators performing tasks affecting product conformity. Instructions reference applicable control plan requirements, identify special characteristics, and are accessible at point of use. Instructions are developed with operator input.
expected_evidence: Work instructions for all production operations
evidence of operator involvement in development/review
current revision at point of use

requirements.title: Verification of Job Setups
requirements.intent: Job setups are verified using last-off part comparison, first article verification, or statistical methods before production begins. Setup records are retained. Tooling is identified and managed.

requirements.title: Verification After Shutdown
requirements.intent: After planned or unplanned shutdowns, product and process verification is performed before resuming production to confirm continued conformity.
failure_modes: no checklist or approval required after shutdown
unplanned shutdowns not subject to same controls as planned

requirements.title: Production Scheduling
requirements.intent: Production is scheduled to meet customer requirements including: customer-specified delivery requirements, just-in-time (JIT) production, and demand-driven scheduling. Schedule adherence is monitored.
expected_evidence: customer delivery requirements reflected in schedule
failure_modes: Scheduling does not reflect customer delivery requirements

requirements.title: Identification and Traceability — Supplemental
requirements.intent: All products are identified throughout production including conformance status. Traceability requirements include lot/batch and, where required, serial number. Customer-mandated traceability requirements implemented.

requirements.title: Production Process Changes — Customer Notification
requirements.intent: Changes to production processes, materials, or suppliers that could affect customer-approved product or process are submitted for customer approval before implementation. Customer notification requirements per applicable CSR are followed.
expected_evidence: customer-notifiable change criteria defined per CSR
customer approval records for process changes
failure_modes: no defined criteria for customer-notifiable changes
requirements.applicability: All organizations supplying to customers with change notification requirements (virtually all automotive OEMs).

requirements.title: Acceptance Criteria
requirements.intent: Acceptance criteria for product conformity are documented and approved by the customer where required. Zero-defect acceptance criteria apply for special characteristics. Criteria are consistent with PPAP-approved samples.
expected_evidence: criteria accessible at point of inspection
failure_modes: criteria not accessible at point of use

requirements.title: Layout Inspection and Functional Testing
requirements.intent: Layout inspection (complete measurement of all drawing characteristics) and functional testing are conducted at frequency required by customer or control plan. Results are retained and reported to customer when required.
expected_evidence: results reported to customer per requirements
